ITQAN:v2p566/r33.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p566/r33.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p566/r33.claim: الأمشاج is the plural of مشيج.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r1.claim: This surah pairs with Qiyamah and its first three verses dovetail with that surah's last four; both establish Judgment, though with different arguments.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r1.anchor: one will realize that they dovetail into one another

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r2.claim: Qiyamah argues from the inward reproaching soul, whereas this surah argues from human creation and the need to reward gratitude and punish ingratitude.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r2.anchor: the chiding soul present within man

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r3.speaker: some maṣāḥif
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r3.claim: Some muṣḥafs classify the surah as Medinan.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r3.anchor: In some ma ṣāḥif , this sūrah is regarded

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r4.claim: Islahi rejects a Medinan classification for every verse, saying subject matter is the criterion and this surah's subject confirms it is wholly Meccan.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r4.anchor: not even one verse of this sūrah was revealed

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r5.claim: For a time man was nonexistent; God created him from a drop through stages into a hearing, understanding being, endowed with awareness of good and evil and tested for gratitude.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p86/r5.anchor: for a certain period of time he was a non-entity

QUSHAYRI:v3p373/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p373/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p373/r5.claim: The mixed drop combines fluid from man and woman; the human passes through stages of drop, clot, bone, and flesh.
QUSHAYRI:v3p373/r5.anchor: { أمشاج } : أخلاط من بين الرجل والمرأة

QUSHAYRI:v3p373/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p373/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p373/r6.claim: Nabtali means that God tests and examines the human being.
QUSHAYRI:v3p373/r6.anchor: { نبتليه } : نمتحنه ونختبره . وقد مضى معناه

QUSHAYRI:v3p373/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p373/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p373/r7.claim: God makes the human able to hear and see.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p355/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p355/r1.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p355/r1.claim: Amshaj means mixed substances; Ibn al-Aʿrabi gives several forms for the word, and the author adduces poetry as evidence for its use.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p355/r1.anchor: الأمشاج: الأخلاط، واحدها مشج بفتحتين، أو مشج كعدل، أو مشيج كشريف وأشراف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p355/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p355/r2.speaker: رؤبة والهذلي والشماخ
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p355/r2.claim: The cited verses by Ruʾba, a Hudhali poet, and al-Shammakh attest the vocabulary of mixed substances.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p355/r2.anchor: الأمشاج: الأخلاط، واحدها مشج بفتحتين، أو مشج كعدل، أو مشيج كشريف وأشراف، قاله ابن الأعرابي، وقال رؤبة:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p356/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p356/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p356/r1.claim: The verb mashaja means to mix; mashij and mamthunj likewise mean mixed, as the cited poem about a drink’s blend illustrates.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p356/r1.anchor: ويقال: مشج يمشج مشجا إذا خلط، ومشيج: كخليط، وممثنوج: كمخلوط

FARRA:v3p213#2/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p213#2/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p213#2/r3.claim: Amshāj are mixtures: male and female fluid, blood, and the clinging clot; mashīj means mixed, like khalīṭ.
FARRA:v3p213#2/r3.anchor: الأمشاج: الأخلاط، ماء الرجل، وماء المرأة، والدم، والعلقة،

FARRA:v3p213#2/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p213#2/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p213#2/r4.claim: The sequence is delayed in meaning: God made the human hearing and sight in order to test him.
FARRA:v3p213#2/r4.anchor: وقوله: نبتليه (2) والمعنى والله أعلم: جعلناه سميعا بصيرا لنبتليه، فهذه مقدمة معناها التأخير.

MAJAZ:v2p279/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p279/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p279/r2.claim: Amshāj means two mixed fluids; Ruʾbah's and Abū Dhuʾayb's poems attest the term.
MAJAZ:v2p279/r2.anchor:
«أمشاج» (2) خلطين قال رؤبة:
من دم أمشاج
[923] وقال أبو ذؤيب:
كأن الريش والفوقين منه ... خلاف النصل سيط به مشيج

BAYDAWI-FULL:76:1-2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:76:1-2/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:76:1-2/r3.claim: أمشاج means mixed components: male and female semen differ in parts and properties, each producing an organ; alternatives are a singular form, different colors, or developmental stages from drop to clot to morsel.
BAYDAWI-FULL:76:1-2/r3.anchor: { أمشاج } أخلاط جمع مشج أو مشج أو مشيج من مشجت الشيء إذا خلطته

BAYDAWI-FULL:76:1-2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:76:1-2/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:76:1-2/r4.claim: نبتليه is circumstantial: God intends to test the human or moves him from one state to another, metaphorically called testing.
BAYDAWI-FULL:76:1-2/r4.anchor: { نبتليه } في موضع الحال أي مبتلين له بمعنى مريدين اختباره أو ناقلين له من حال

BAYDAWI-FULL:76:1-2/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:76:1-2/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:76:1-2/r5.claim: Hearing and sight enable recognition of signs and listening to revelations, resulting from the test and introduced by فاء.
BAYDAWI-FULL:76:1-2/r5.anchor: { فجعلنه سميعا بصيرا } ليتمكن من مشاهدة الدلائل واستماع الآيات

NAHHAS:v5p95/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p95/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p95/r3.claim: Amshāj may be an adjective of nuṭfah without ellipsis, the veins in semen; alternatively male and female fluids are mixed and both called nuṭfah, or it means clot and flesh with an implied 'having mixtures.'
NAHHAS:v5p95/r3.anchor: ( أمشاج ) من نعت نطفة على غير حذف في قول من قال الأمشاج العروق

NAHHAS:v5p95/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p95/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p95/r4.claim: Mishīj is singular of amshāj like sharīf/ashrāf; mashaj is another form like ʿadl/aʿdāl.
NAHHAS:v5p95/r4.anchor: وواحدتهما مشيج مثل شريف وأشراف ويقال مشج مثل عدل وأعدال

NAHHAS:v5p95/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p95/r5.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v5p95/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ parses the phrase as fronted: God made the human hearing and seeing in order to test him.
NAHHAS:v5p95/r5.anchor: قال الفراء هو على التقديم والتأخير والمعنى عنده جعلنا الإنسان سميعا بصيرا لنبتليه

NAHHAS:v5p95/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p95/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p95/r6.claim: Abu Jaʿfar rejects the fronting: faʾ orders the events, senses are needed for testing, and the passage lists divine favors without a purposive lām.
NAHHAS:v5p95/r6.anchor: وقال من خالفه في هذا هو خطأ من غير جهة فمنها أنه لا يكون مع الفاء تقديم ولا تأخير

BIQAI-FULL:v8p260/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p260/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p260/r1.claim: Biqāʿī places the passage after the deniers’ prideful rejection of resurrection, contrasting that posture with reflection on humanity’s humble origin.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p260/r1.anchor: ولما تقدم في القيامة إخباره تعالى عن حال منكري البعث عنادا واستكبارا وتعاميا عن النظر والاعتبار

BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r1.claim: The Creator formed varied bones, joints, tendons, and ligaments, specifying their shapes and counts so the body can move and remain sound.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r1.anchor: وقدرها بمقادير وأشكال مختلفة , فمنها صغير وكبير

BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r2.claim: Distinct senses and organs serve precise purposes: eyes convey images, ears gather sound, the nose detects scents, teeth divide food, and the tongue expresses thought.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r2.anchor: ففتح العين ورتب طبقاتها وأحسن شكلها ولونها وأحكمها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r3.claim: Internal organs divide the work of digestion and circulation; the entire intricate body begins as a tiny drop in three layers of darkness, proving its unseen Maker.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r3.anchor: وكان مبدأ ذلك كله النطفة على صغرها في داخل الرحمن في ظلمات ثلاثة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r4.claim: People marvel at a fine design on a wall yet overlook the Creator of the far greater wonders in themselves and others.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r4.anchor: فسبحانه ما أعظم شأنه وأبهر برهانه , فيالله العجب ممن يرى نقشا حسنا على جدار فيتعجب من حسنه

DURR-FULL:v8p366/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p366/r10.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p366/r10.claim: Ibn Masud connects the Quran with embryonic stages: after forty days each as a drop and clot, an angel writes sex, destiny, provision, effects, and term; he glosses amshaj as the embryo's veins.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p372/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p372/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p372/r3.claim: The next statement answers the suspenseful rhetorical question: God brought humanity into being after nonexistence, first creating a reproductive drop.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p372/r3.anchor: والتقرير يقتضي الإقرار بذلك لا محالة لأنه معلوم بالضرورة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p372/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p372/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p372/r4.claim: The emphatic particle treats idolaters as deniers of God's creation because they worship objects that did not create them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p372/r4.anchor: وتأكيد الكلام بحرف ( إن ) لتنزيل المشركين منزلة من ينكر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p372/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p372/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p372/r5.claim: ‘The human’ denotes the whole human kind, and the account of reproductive creation embeds evidence of divine knowledge, power, and wisdom.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p372/r5.anchor: والمراد ب { الإنسان } مثل ما أريد به في قوله : { هل أتى على الإنسان }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p372/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p372/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p372/r6.claim: Amshaj derives from mixing: it describes a mixed drop, as creation of pairs from earthly growth and other sources illustrates.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p372/r6.anchor: مشتق من المشج وهو الخلط ، أي نطفة مخلوطة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p372/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p372/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p372/r7.claim: Al-Farra, Ibn al-Sikkit, and al-Mubarrad take amshaj as a plural form, with possible singular patterns meaning ‘mixed.’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p372/r7.anchor: وعلى ذلك حملها الفراء وابن السكيت والمبرد ، فهي إما جمع مشج

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p161/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p161/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p161/r13.claim: Here الإنسان means every descendant of Adam, according to all commentators.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p161/r13.anchor: يعني بالإنسان في هذا الموضع كل إنسان من بني آدم في قول جميع المفسرين

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p161/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p161/r14.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p161/r14.claim: The nutfa may be the man's and woman's fluids once mixed together.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p161/r14.anchor: أحدهما : ماء الرجل وماء المرأة إذا اختلطا فهما نطفة , قاله السدي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p161/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p161/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p161/r15.claim: Alternatively, nutfa is the man's fluid; once it mixes with the woman's fluid in the womb, the two become amshaj.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p161/r15.anchor: الثاني : أن النطفة ماء الرجل , فإذا اختلط في الرحم وماء المرأة صارا أمشاجا .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p161/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p161/r16.speaker: الحسن وعكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p161/r16.claim: One explanation of amshaj is mixtures: the man's fluid mixed with the woman's.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p161/r16.anchor: أحدها : أنه الأخلاط ، وهو أن يختلط ماء الرجل بماء المرأة ، قاله الحسن وعكرمة ،

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p161/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p161/r17.speaker: رؤبة بن العجاج
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p161/r17.claim: Ruba's cited verse is offered as linguistic evidence for the term amshaj; the excerpt ends before the line is given.

MUQATIL:76:1-3/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:76:1-3/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:76:1-3/r2.claim: Amshaj is mixed male and female fluid: the thick white male fluid yields nerves, bones, and strength; the thin yellow female fluid yields flesh, blood, hair, and nails.
MUQATIL:76:1-3/r2.anchor: ماء الرجل غليظ أبيض، فمنه العصب، والعظم، والقوة، ونطفة المرأة صفراء رقيقة

MUQATIL:76:1-3/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:76:1-3/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:76:1-3/r3.claim: The mixed drop develops through clot and morsel into a human, made hearing and seeing after being lifeless, so that God may test him.
MUQATIL:76:1-3/r3.anchor: أي جعلناه نطفة، علقة، مضغة، ثم صار إنسانا بعد ماء ودم

QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r5.claim: The human created is Adam’s descendant; nutfa is dripping semen, and by extension any small amount of water held in a vessel.
QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r5.anchor: أي ابن آدم من غير خلاف

QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن رواحة
QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r6.claim: Ibn Rawaha’s poem uses nutfa for a small amount of fluid in a waterskin.
QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r6.anchor: مالي أراك تكرهين الجنه هل أنت إلا نطفة في شنه

QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r7.claim: Amshaj means mixed fluids; its singular forms include mashj and mashij, and a cited line by Ru’ba witnesses to the word.
QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r7.anchor: واحدها: مشج ومشيج، مثل خدن وخدين

QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r8.speaker: المبرد
QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r8.claim: Al-Mubarrad gives mashij as the singular and says the mixture here is semen with blood.
QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r8.anchor: واحد الأمشاج: مشيج يقال: مشج يمشج: إذا خلط

QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r9.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r9.claim: Al-Farra identifies the mixture as the man’s and woman’s fluids, blood, and the clot.
QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r9.anchor: أمشاج: أخلاط ماء الرجل وماء المرأة، والدم والعلقة

QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says amshaj describes red mixed with white, an explanation many language scholars prefer.
QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r10.anchor: الأمشاج: الحمرة في البياض، والبياض في الحمرة

QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r11.claim: Another report says the man’s thick white fluid and woman’s thin yellow fluid combine; sinew, bone, and strength come from the man, while flesh, blood, and hair come from the woman; this is also reported as Prophetic.
QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r11.anchor: فما كان من عصب وعظم وقوة فهو من ماء الرجل، وما كان من لحم ودم وشعر فهو من ماء المرأة

QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r12.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r12.claim: Ibn Masud says amshaj refers to the veins of the embryo, and also identifies it as the two colored male and female fluids.

QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r13.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r13.claim: Mujahid says the man’s semen is white and the woman’s is green or yellow.
QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r13.anchor: نطفة الرجل بيضاء ونطفة المرأة خضراء وصفراء

QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r14.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r14.claim: They describe human creation in stages from dust and reproductive fluid through clot, morsel, bone, and flesh, paralleling al-Mu’minun.
QURTUBI-FULL:76:1-2/r14.anchor: ثم علقة ثم مضغة ثم عظم ثم لحم

ZAJJAJ:v5p257/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p257/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p257/r4.claim: Amshāj means mixtures of semen and blood, moving from one stage to another; its singular is mishīj.
ZAJJAJ:v5p257/r4.anchor: (أمشاج) أخلاط مني ودم، ثم ينقل من حال إلى حال.

ZAJJAJ:v5p257/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p257/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p257/r5.claim: Nabtalī means “test”; the fact that God made the human hearing and seeing demonstrates this testing purpose.

STUDYQURAN:76:1/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:76:1/r1.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:76:1/r1.claim: In verses 1–2, man may refer to Adam, all humanity, or both.
STUDYQURAN:76:1/r1.anchor: refers to Adam, all of humanity (R), or both

TABATABAI:76:1-22#6/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:76:1-22#6/r9.speaker: أبو الجارود
TABATABAI:76:1-22#6/r9.claim: Al-Jarud reports from al-Baqir that “mingled fluids” means the man's and woman's fluids mixed together.
TABATABAI:76:1-22#6/r9.anchor: في رواية أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في قوله تعالى { امشاج نبتليه } قال ماء الرجل والمرأة اختلطا جميعا

TABRISI:76:1-10/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:76:1-10/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:76:1-10/r10.claim: A nuṭfa is a small amount of water but can also denote a large amount; Ali used it for the Nahrawan battlefield and poetry gives an example.
TABRISI:76:1-10/r10.anchor: وأصل النطفة الماء القليل وقد تقع على الكثير

TABRISI:76:1-10/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:76:1-10/r11.speaker: أمير المؤمنين
TABRISI:76:1-10/r11.claim: Ali called the Kharijites' battlefield ‘beyond the nuṭfa,’ meaning the Nahrawan river.
TABRISI:76:1-10/r11.anchor: قال أمير المؤمنين ع حين ذكر الخوارج: مصارعهم دون النطفة يريد النهروان

TABRISI:76:1-10/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:76:1-10/r12.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
TABRISI:76:1-10/r12.claim: The line comparing the soul to a drop in a basin shows nuṭfa can mean a small quantity of fluid.
TABRISI:76:1-10/r12.anchor: وما النفس إلا نطفة بقرارة إذا لم تكدر كان صفوا غديرها

TABRISI:76:1-10#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:76:1-10#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:76:1-10#2/r1.claim: Amshāj means mixtures and is the plural of mashīj or mashj; to mix one thing with another is to mashaja it.
TABRISI:76:1-10#2/r1.anchor: وواحد الأمشاج مشيج ومشجت هذا بهذا أي خلطته وهو ممشوج ومشيج

TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r7.claim: “Human” in “We created the human” means Adam's descendants; the drop is the combined male and female reproductive fluids.
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r7.anchor: يعني ولد آدم ع { من نطفة } وهي ماء الرجل والمرأة الذي يخلق منه الولد

TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r8.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وعكرمة ومجاهد
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r8.claim: Amshaj means male and female fluids mixed in the womb; whichever fluid prevails determines resemblance.
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس والحسن وعكرمة ومجاهد

TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r9.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r9.claim: Amshaj may mean the successive stages from a drop to a clot, a lump, bones, and finally a human.
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r9.anchor: أمشاج أطوار طورا نطفة وطورا علقة وطورا مضغة وطورا عظاما

TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r10.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك والكلبي
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r10.claim: Another interpretation takes amshaj as differing colors in male and female fluids; this is also reported from Ibn Abbas.
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r10.anchor: فهي مختلفة الألوان عن مجاهد والضحاك والكلبي. وروي أيضا عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r11.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r11.claim: Hasan says the drop is mixed with menstrual blood, which ceases when pregnancy begins.
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r11.anchor: نطفة مشجت بدم الحيض فإذا حبلت ارتفع الحيض عن الحسن

TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r12.speaker: ابن مسعود
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r12.claim: Ibn Masud interprets amshaj as the veins within the reproductive fluid.
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r12.anchor: هي العروق التي تكون في النطفة عن ابن مسعود

TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r13.claim: Amshaj can also mean the temperamental mixtures of heat, cold, dryness, and moisture, balanced into an animal body and then given life, hearing, and sight.
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r13.anchor: أخلاط من الطبائع التي تكون في الإنسان من الحرارة والبرودة واليبوسة والرطوبة

TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r14.claim: God tests people through difficult obligations to make obedience or disobedience evident and recompense them accordingly.
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r14.anchor: أي نختبره بما نكلفه من الأفعال الشاقة ليظهر إما طاعته وإما عصيانه

TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r15.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r15.claim: Al-Farra connects being given hearing and sight with the test: these faculties let people receive commands and prohibitions.
TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r15.anchor: قال الفراء معناه { فجعلناه سميعا بصيرا } لنبتليه أي لنتعبده

THALABI:v10p93#3/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p93#3/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p93#3/r4.claim: Nutfah means the man's and woman's seminal fluid, and more generally any small amount of liquid in a container; its root refers to dripping and it has plural forms nutaf and niṭāf.
THALABI:v10p93#3/r4.anchor: إنا خلقنا الإنسان يعني ولد آدم من نطفة يعني من مني الرجل ومني المرأة، وكل ماء قليل في وعاء

THALABI:v10p93#3/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p93#3/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p93#3/r5.claim: Ibn Rawaha's line illustrates nutfah, while the root's sense of dripping explains the word.
THALABI:v10p93#3/r5.anchor: كقول عبد الله بن رواحة: هل أنت إلا نطفة، وجمعها نطاف ونطف

THALABI:v10p93#3/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p93#3/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p93#3/r6.claim: Amshaj means mixtures; mashj and mashij are singular forms, and the word can describe something mixed.
THALABI:v10p93#3/r6.anchor: أمشاج أخلاط، واحدها مشج مشيج مثل حذن وحذين

THALABI:v10p93#3/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p93#3/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p93#3/r7.claim: Rujba's poem illustrates amshaj as fluids mixed with blood, and Abu Duad's line illustrates mashij as blended parts.
THALABI:v10p93#3/r7.anchor: يطرحن كل معجل نساج … لم يكس جلدا في دم أمشاج

THALABI:v10p93#3/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p93#3/r8.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وعكرمة ومجاهد والربيع
THALABI:v10p93#3/r8.claim: They say the man's thick white fluid and woman's thin yellow fluid mix in the womb; whichever prevails determines the child's resemblance.
THALABI:v10p93#3/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس والحسن وعكرمة ومجاهد والربيع: يعني ماء الرجل وماء المرأة يختلطان في الرحم

THALABI:v10p93#3/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p93#3/r9.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v10p93#3/r9.claim: Qatada interprets amshaj as the stages of development from fluid to clot, morsel, flesh and bones, then a new creation.

THALABI:v10p93#3/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p93#3/r10.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v10p93#3/r10.claim: Al-Dahhak says the fluids differ in color; reports through al-Wali from Ibn Abbas and Ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid agree, as do Ata al-Khurasani and al-Kalbi.
THALABI:v10p93#3/r10.anchor: وقال الضحاك: أراد اختلاف ألوان النطفة

THALABI:v10p93#3/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p93#3/r11.speaker: عطاء الخراساني والكلبي
THALABI:v10p93#3/r11.claim: Ata al-Khurasani and al-Kalbi describe amshaj as red mixed with white, or white mixed with red or yellow.
THALABI:v10p93#3/r11.anchor: وكذلك قال عطاء الخراساني والكلبي: الأمشاج الحمرة في البياض والبياض في الحمرة أو الصفرة

THALABI:v10p94/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p94/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود وأسامة بن زيد
THALABI:v10p94/r1.claim: Ibn Masud and Usama ibn Zayd say amshaj refers to veins within the fluid.
THALABI:v10p94/r1.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن مسعود وأسامة بن زيد: هي العروق التي تكون في النطفة

THALABI:v10p94/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p94/r2.speaker: ابن جريج عن عطاء
THALABI:v10p94/r2.claim: A report from Ata through Ibn Jurayj describes amshaj as thin strands resembling sinew.
THALABI:v10p94/r2.anchor: وروى ابن جريح عن عطاء قال: الأمشاج الهن الذي كأنه عقب

THALABI:v10p94/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p94/r3.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v10p94/r3.claim: Hasan says the fluid is mixed with menstrual blood, which stops when pregnancy occurs.
THALABI:v10p94/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن: نعم والله خلقت من نطفة مشجت بدم وهو دم الحيضة

THALABI:v10p94/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p94/r4.speaker: يمان
THALABI:v10p94/r4.claim: Yaman defines amshaj as any two colors mixed together.
THALABI:v10p94/r4.anchor: وقال يمان: كل لونين اختلطا فهما أمشاج

THALABI:v10p94/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p94/r5.speaker: ابن السكيت
THALABI:v10p94/r5.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit calls amshaj mixtures of substances, explaining that humans inherit varied dispositions from them.

THALABI:v10p94/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p94/r6.speaker: أهل المعاني
THALABI:v10p94/r6.claim: The grammarians say amshaj has a plural pattern but a singular sense because it describes one fluid, like other collective adjectives.
THALABI:v10p94/r6.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: بناء الأمشاج بناء جمع وهو في معنى الواحد

THALABI:v10p94/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p94/r7.speaker: أبو عثمان المغربي
THALABI:v10p94/r7.claim: Abu Uthman al-Maghribi gives a mystical reading of nine inner mixtures: senses are tempting, self, desire, and Satan pull toward unbelief, while intellect, spirit, and angel support faith; divine aid lets intellect govern the heart and subdue desire.
THALABI:v10p94/r7.anchor: سمعت أبا عبد الرحمن السلمي يقول: سمعت أبا عثمان المغربي يقول: سئلت وأنا بمكة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:76:1-3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:76:1-3/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:76:1-3/r2.claim: Adam's descendants were made from the mixed fluids of man and woman, including their differing colors, to be tested by commands and prohibitions.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:76:1-3/r2.anchor: { إنا خلقنا الإنسان } يعني: ابن آدم { من نطفة أمشاج } أخلاط، يعني: ماء الرجل وماء المرأة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p299/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p299/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p299/r3.claim: The opening question prompts assent and then asks who created humanity; the answer's emphatic innā and fronted subject convey that God alone created humans.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p299/r3.anchor: فهو الخالق حصرا ليس معه شريك سبحانه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p299/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p299/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p299/r4.claim: The shared first-person subject of creating, testing, and granting hearing and sight shows that God both creates and tests humanity and supplies the means of the test.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p299/r4.anchor: الخالق والمبتلي جهة واحدة وهو الله تعالى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p300/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p300/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p300/r1.claim: The author identifies the first verse's human as Adam and the next verse's human as Adam's descendants, whose creation from a mixed drop shows divine power and continued human generation.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p300/r1.anchor: في الآية الثانية ذرية آدم - عليه السلام - فذكر الإنسان الأول ومن بعده

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p356/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p356/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p356/r1.claim: The opening uses inna because initial creation from nothing, the beginning of reproductive succession, and creation for testing are difficult and contested; ordinary creation through parents is widely acknowledged.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p356/r1.anchor: الآية في أول السورة احتاجت إلى توكيد فجاء بـ (إن)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p356/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p356/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p356/r2.claim: Disbelievers also contest creation for testing and judgment, so the verse's mention of نبتليه adds another disputed claim requiring emphasis.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p356/r2.anchor: كفار قريش كانوا ينكرون هذا ويقولون هل خلق الله الإنسان ليبتليه ثم يحاسبه

ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r8.claim: Raghib defines “nuṭfa” as pure water; the word also denotes male fluid and is commonly treated as synonymous with semen.

ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r9.claim: The Qur’an calls the nuṭfa a part of semen, and a Muslim report likewise says a child does not come from all of the fluid but from a portion of it.
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r9.anchor: diye nutfenin meniden bir cüz olduğu ifade olunmuş

ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r10.claim: The general statement that humanity comes from a nuṭfa appears to include Adam, while requiring that his nuṭfa did not come from another human; his beginning is from clay.
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r10.anchor: Sonra insan cinsinin bir nutfeden yaratılmış olmasının zâhiri Âdem’in de bir nutfeden yaratılmış olduğunu ifade eder.

ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r11.claim: Although 3:59 might suggest excluding Adam, the dust and clay verses describe humanity’s origin and do not contradict Adam’s beginning from a nonhuman nuṭfa; the general wording excludes no person.
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r11.anchor: gibi umûma hitab eden âyetler de mebde’ nokta-i nazarından bunların bütün insanlar hakkında sâdık olduğunu anlattığından

ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r12.claim: “Amshāj” comes from a root meaning to mix, but exegetes dispute whether it is singular or plural.
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r12.anchor: “Emşâc”: “Nutfe”ye sıfat yapılan bu kelime, bir şeyi bir şeye karıştırmak

ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r13.speaker: Sâhib-Keşşâf
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r13.claim: Al-Zamakhshari in al-Kashshaf prefers a singular adjective for the singular nuṭfa, meaning mixed, and rejects treating the form as a plural.
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r13.anchor: Sâhib-Keşşâf müfred olan “nutfe”ye sıfat olduğu için

ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r14.claim: The apparent form is plural, with singulars like meşec, meşic, or meşic; most exegetes gloss it as mixtures.

ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r15.claim: As a singular it pictures one mixture of combined parts; as a plural it pictures multiple mixtures whose components are themselves mixtures.
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r15.anchor: müfrede sıfat olması “zâti emşâcin” takdîrinde olarak emşâclı yahut ahlâttan ibaret

ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r16.claim: “Ahlāṭ” are mixed fluids such as blood, bile, phlegm, and lymph; the nuṭfa’s complete composition is known only to its Maker.
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r16.anchor: kan, safra, sevdâ, balgam “lenfa” (lymphe) gibi karışık kimyevî mürekkebât-ı mahsûsaya “ahlât” ıtlak olunur.

ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r17.claim: Many understand the mixture as male and female fluids combining in the womb at fertilization, but Elmalılı considers this too late because the product is then called an embryo or clinging clot.
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r17.anchor: ihtilâtı, yani telkīh hâli diye telakkī etmişlerdir.

ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r18.claim: Others explain the mixtures as blood and similar humors.
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r18.anchor: Bazıları da kan ve emsâli ahlât demişlerdir.

ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r19.speaker: İbn Mes‘ûd
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r19.claim: Ibn Masud is reported to explain the nuṭfa’s “roots” or essential lines; Elmalılı reads these as formative traits embedded in the germ cell.

ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r20.speaker: Katâde
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r20.claim: Qatada is reported to explain “amshāj” as colors and stages; Elmalılı applies this to the successive stages before conception and in embryonic development.

ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r21.claim: Humanity is neither self-existent and perfect nor made as a simple creature in one instant; it develops through long stages as earlier, unrecognized materials are filtered, mixed, and cultivated.
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r21.anchor: dehrin bidâyetinden beri devir devir, tavır tavır yaratılagelmiş gayr-i mezkur şeylerin süzülüp birbirlerine katıla katıla

ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r22.claim: The complex nuṭfa and the vast development from it to a human cannot arise from autonomous nature; nature is dependent, while the Creator wills, composes, and cultivates.
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r22.anchor: hüküm tabiatın değil, ona hâkim olan Hâlık ve Sâni‘Hak teâlâ’nındır

ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r23.claim: God created the human to test him with responsibilities, duties, senses, and hardships, not to leave him purposeless; this links to 67:2 and 75:40.
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r23.anchor: onu mübtelâ kılmak üzere evire çevire yani o insanı öyle yaratıp artık bitti diye südâ ve mühmel bırakıvermek için değil

ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r24.speaker: author
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r24.claim: God made the human hearing and seeing so he can perceive revealed and created signs, understand through insight, and fulfill his responsibilities.
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r24.anchor: tenzîlî, tekvînî âyât ve delâili işitecek, görecek, basîretle bilip ona göre şuur ile vazifesini yapacak

ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r25.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r25.speaker: author
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r25.claim: After many stages, the human receives a distinct spiritual creation and remains a traveler through life, death, and a further life; this connects to 71:14 and 23:14.
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r25.anchor: bambaşka[^16] bir rûhânî hilkate mazhar edilmiş, semî‘basîr mevt ve hayat geçitleriyle mübtelâ

ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r26.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r26.speaker: author
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r26.claim: One who does not truly hear, see, and consider duties to the Lord is unworthy of the title “human”; this definition is deeper than “rational animal.”
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r26.anchor: hakkıyla semî‘basîr olmayan ve Rabbine karşı vazifelerini düşünmeyen kimseler “insan” unvânına lâyık değildirler.

ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r27.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r27.speaker: author
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r27.claim: The testing clause gathers Qur’anic obligations, especially the human trials, hardship, reward, and punishment described in al-Mulk, al-Qiyama, and later surahs.
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r27.anchor: نَّبْتَلِيهِ kaydı umumiyetle Kur’an’da beyan olunagelen mükellefiyetlerin hepsine işaret olmakla beraber

ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r28.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r28.speaker: author
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r28.claim: The description “seeing” specially recalls the statement that the human is a witness against himself in 75:14.
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r28.anchor: بَصِيرًا vasfının yine Sûre-i Kıyâme’de geçen

ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r29.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r29.speaker: Hazret-i Sıddîk
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r29.claim: Al-Razi reports that Abu Bakr wished the human’s creation had ended before the testing stage, expressing his awareness of human incompleteness and the burden of future duties.
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r29.anchor: Hazret-i Sıddîk bu âyeti işittiği vakit يَا لَيْتـَهَا كَانَتْ تَمَّتْ فَلاَ نـُبْتـَلَى

ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r30.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r30.speaker: author
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r30.claim: These verses condense humanity’s delayed creation, successive refinement, spiritual nature, dependence on the Creator, and destiny under a law of testing and responsibility.
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r30.anchor: bu iki âyet insanın hilkat tarihinde hikmet-i teahhuru, geçirdiği ıstıfâ mertebeleriyle sûret-i tekvîni hâli ve istikbâli

ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r31.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r31.speaker: author
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r31.claim: Although death does not exhaust human destiny, the human travels toward the Lord and toward either the Fire or bliss, as stated in 75:30 and 75:12.
ELMALILI:76:1-4#2/r31.anchor: إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ ٱلْمَسَاقُ ve إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ ٱلْمُسْتَقَرُّ

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:1/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:1/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:1/r6.claim: Each person was once nonexistent, then began as sperm and ovum joined into an embryo; endowed with hearing and sight, the person becomes capable of responsibility and trial.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:1/r6.anchor: Bu ikisinin birleşmesiyle ana rahminde bir embriyo haline gelmektedir

BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r1.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r1.claim: Inwardly, the human has an unseen conceptual form and a visible concrete form, both eternally known to God; His prior knowledge encompasses all things, which manifest His names and attributes.
BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r1.anchor: للإنسان صورة علمية غيبية وصورة عينية شهادية وهو من حيث كلتا الصورتين مذكور عند الله أزلا وأبدا

BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r2.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r2.claim: The question whether a time passed when the human was forgotten is answered negatively: all are present to God’s knowledge, including the human created in His image; only the veiled fail to recognize this.
BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r2.anchor: وهل للاستفهام الإنكاري بخلاف المحجوبين عن علم المعرفة والحكمة الإلهية

BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r3.speaker: جعفر الصادق
BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r3.claim: Ja‘far al-Sadiq glosses the question as asking whether there was ever a time when God was not remembering the human.
BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r3.anchor: هل أتى عليك يا إنسان وقت لم يكن الله ذاكرا لك فيه

BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r4.claim: ‘We created the human’ means the body; explicit naming reinforces the statement. The nutfa develops into a clot at forty days, a morsel at eighty, and receives the spirit at one hundred twenty.
BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r4.anchor: أي خلقناه يعني جسمه والإظهار لزيادة التقرير

BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r5.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r5.claim: A report from al-Dahhak through Ibn Abbas says Adam’s creation proceeded through forty years each in clay, dark mud, and baked clay before the spirit was breathed into him; what took Adam years took descendants days.
BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r5.anchor: سنين في آدم كان أياما في أولاده

BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r6.claim: Some take the first human as Adam and the second as his descendants, with ‘time’ an unknown long duration; the author prefers ‘human’ to mean the species in both places, recalling its origin from nothing and humble fluid to rebut denial of resurrection.
BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r6.anchor: وحمل بعضهم الإنسان الأول على آدم والثاني على أولاده

BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r7.claim: Amshaj means mixed elements; it is a plural-form adjective for the single nutfa because the intended matter combines male and female fluids, whose colors, consistencies, and properties differ.
BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r7.anchor: جمع مشج كسبب أو كتف على

BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r8.claim: The author says the male fluid is white and thick and the female fluid yellow and thin; the child resembles whichever prevails, with nerves, bones, and strength from the male and flesh, blood, and hair from the female, according to a Prophetic report.
BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r8.anchor: ماء الرجل أبيض غليظ فيه قوة العقد

BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r9.speaker: رسول الله
BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r9.claim: A report says each newborn has some of the soil of its burial place mixed into its nutfa.
BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r9.anchor: ما من مولدو إلا وقد ذر على نطفته من تربة حفرته

BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r10.speaker: الحسن
BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r10.claim: Al-Hasan says the mixed nutfa includes menstrual blood, which stops when pregnancy begins; al-Qamus likewise defines it as mixed with the woman’s fluid and blood.
BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r10.anchor: نطفة مشيجة بدم وهو دم الحيض فإذا حبلت ارتفع الحيض

BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r11.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r11.claim: Al-Raghib interprets the mixture as the different powers God placed in the nutfa, pointing to the successive stages of creation in 23:12–14.
BURSEVI:v10p200#3/r11.anchor: هو عبارة عما جعل الله بالنطفة من القوى المختلفة المشار إليها بقوله

BURSEVI:v10p201/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p201/r1.speaker: قتادة
BURSEVI:v10p201/r1.claim: Qatada says amshaj means colors and stages.
BURSEVI:v10p201/r1.anchor: فيكون معنى أمشاج ألوان وأطوار على ما قال قتادة

BURSEVI:v10p201/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p201/r2.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v10p201/r2.claim: Inwardly, the mixed nutfa is the interweaving of receptive potential and active power, represented by the most holy and holy effusions, respectively likened to male and female fluids.
BURSEVI:v10p201/r2.anchor: أي من نطفة قوة القابلية الممتشجة المختلطة بنطفة قوة الفاعلية أي خلقناه من نطفة الفيض الأقدس

BURSEVI:v10p201/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p201/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p201/r3.claim: ‘Testing him’ is a prospective state: God intends to test through future obligations, making people’s acceptance, rejection, felicity, and misery manifest in detail after being known generally.
BURSEVI:v10p201/r3.anchor: حال مقدرة من فاعل خلقنا أي مريدين ابتلاءه واختباره

BURSEVI:v10p201/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p201/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p201/r4.claim: Hearing and sight equip a person to hear revealed signs and witness created signs, enabling the intended test; intellect is omitted because the passage names its instruments and usual route to completion.
BURSEVI:v10p201/r4.anchor: ليتمكن من استماع الآيات التنزيلية ومشاهدة الآيات التكوينية

BURSEVI:v10p201/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p201/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p201/r5.claim: The intensive forms signal the completeness of God’s favor; ‘seeing’ is the second object after the first object of ‘made.’
BURSEVI:v10p201/r5.anchor: وفي اختيار صيغة المبالغة إشارة إلى كمال إحسنه إليه وتمام إنعامه

BURSEVI:v10p201/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p201/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v10p201/r6.claim: Inwardly, God becomes the servant’s hearing and sight: by Him the servant hears and sees every audible and visible thing, with nothing escaping perception.
BURSEVI:v10p201/r6.anchor: كما قال كنت سمعه وبصره فبي يسمع وبي يبصر فلا يفوته شيء من المسموعات

BURSEVI:v10p201/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p201/r7.speaker: أبو عثمان المغربي
BURSEVI:v10p201/r7.claim: Abu Uthman al-Maghribi describes nine inner mixtures: hearing, sight, and tongue tempt; ego, desire, and Satan oppose faith; intellect, spirit, and heart believe.
BURSEVI:v10p201/r7.anchor: وقال أبو عثمان المغربي قدس سره ابتلى الله الخلق بتسعة أمشاج

BURSEVI:v10p201/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p201/r8.speaker: أبو عثمان المغربي
BURSEVI:v10p201/r8.claim: With divine aid, intellect masters the heart, captures ego and desire, and makes the self kin to spirit and desire kin to intellect, so God’s word prevails; he cites the command to fight until there is no fitna.
BURSEVI:v10p201/r8.anchor: فإذا أيد الله العبد بالمعونة قهر العقل على

SULAMI:v2p363#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p363#2/r1.speaker: أبو عثمان المغربي
SULAMI:v2p363#2/r1.claim: God tests people through nine components: hearing, sight, and tongue tempt; the self, enemy, and passion disbelieve; reason, spirit, and heart believe; divine help lets reason master the heart and restrain self and passion.
SULAMI:v2p363#2/r1.anchor: سمعت أبا عثمان المغربي يقول : سئلت وأنا بمكة عن قول الله ﴿ أمشاج نبتليه ﴾ فقلت : ابتلاء الله بتسعة أمشاج

AKHFASH:v2p558/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p558/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p558/r4.claim: The singular of أمشاج is المشج.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p502#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p502#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p502#3/r1.claim: أمشاج means mixtures: the man's fluid mixed with the woman's fluid; مشيج is a mixed thing.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p502#3/r1.anchor: مشجته فهو مشيج. يريد: اختلاط ماء الرجل

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p502#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p502#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p502#3/r2.claim: نبتليه means We test him; God made the human hearing and seeing in order to test him through them.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p502#3/r2.anchor: نختبره. أي إنا جعلناه سميعا بصيرا

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3390#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3390#2/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3390#2/r1.claim: Ibn Mas'ud glosses amshaj as veins.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3390#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود في قوله : امشاج قال : العروق

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3390#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3390#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3390#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the mixed drop is formed when the man's fluid and the woman's fluid combine.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3390#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : من نطفة امشاج قال : من ماء الرجل وماء المراة حين يختلطان

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3390#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3390#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3390#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas also glosses amshaj as varied in color.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3390#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : من نطفة امشاج قال : مختلفة الالوان

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3390#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3390#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3390#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas describes amshaj as cord-like material that comes after urine, from which a child develops.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3390#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : الامشاج الذي يخرج على اثر البول كقطع الاوتار ومنه يكون الولد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p374/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p374/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p374/r1.claim: Following al-Zamakhsharī, Ibn ʿĀshūr prefers treating amshāj as a singular with a plural-like form, directly modifying nutfa; he thinks Sibawayh does not explicitly forbid this and notes Zamakhsharī's close adherence to him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p374/r1.anchor: والوجه ما ذهب إليه صاحب ( الكشاف ) : أن { أمشاج } مفرد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p374/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p374/r2.speaker: الفراء وابن السكيت والمبرد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p374/r2.claim: They treat amshāj as a plural; the singular semen is described by the varied properties of its components, each contributing to body parts, intensifying the description as strongly mixed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p374/r2.anchor: وإذا كان جمعا كما جرى عليه كلام الفراء وابن السكيت والمبرد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p374/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p374/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p374/r3.claim: The mixed components include chemical, vegetal, or earthy elements and elements of vital force.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p374/r3.anchor: وهذه الأمشاج منها ما هو أجزاء كيمائية نباتية أو ترابية ومنها ما هو عناصر قوى الحياة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p374/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p374/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p374/r4.claim: “Testing him” is a prospective circumstantial clause: testing means later obligation after rational maturity; it is moved forward for emphasis, although it logically follows guidance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p374/r4.anchor: وجملة { نبتليه } في موضع الحال من الإنسان وهي حال مقدرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p375/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p375/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p375/r1.claim: Human hearing and sight are foundational to thinking and judgment; the intensive forms reflect humans' greater perception and discrimination than animals'.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p375/r1.anchor: ولذلك جاء وصفه بالسميع البصير بصيغة المبالغة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p375/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p375/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p375/r2.claim: Hearing receives religious law and prophetic calls, while sight examines proofs of God's existence and artistry.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p375/r2.anchor: فبالسمع يتلقى الشرائع ودعوة الرسل وبالبصر ينظر في أدلة وجود الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p375/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p375/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p375/r3.claim: Being made subject to religious duties and law distinguishes humanity, grounds civilization, and leads into the statement that God guided the way.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p375/r3.anchor: وهذا تخلص إلى ما ميز الله به الإنسان من جعله تجاه التكليف واتباع الشرائع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p408#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p408#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p408#2/r7.claim: الإنسان in the creation statement is generic because Adam was not made from a drop.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p408#2/r7.anchor: وقوله تعالى: إنا خلقنا الإنسان هو هنا اسم الجنس بلا خلاف. لأن آدم لم يخلق من نطفة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p408#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p408#2/r8.speaker: ابن السكيت وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p408#2/r8.claim: أمشاج means mixed substances, with singular مشج whose م and ش are both open.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p408#2/r8.anchor: وأمشاج معناه أخلاط واحدها مشج بفتح الميم والشين قاله ابن السكيت وغيره،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p408#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p408#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p408#2/r9.claim: One singular form is مشج, like عدل.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r1.claim: The singular مشيج follows the pattern of شريف; the preceding segment compared another singular form with عدل.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r1.anchor: وأعدال، وقيل: مشيج مثل شريف وأشراف،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r2.speaker: آخرون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r2.claim: One account explains the mixture as the man's fluid mixed with the woman's.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r2.anchor: واختلف في المقصود من الخلط، فقيل هو أمشاج ماء الرجل بماء المرأة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r3.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r3.claim: Al-Tabari transmits a report, also in some compilations, that bones and sinew come from the man's fluid and flesh and fat from the woman's.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r3.anchor: وأسند الطبري حديثا وهو أيضا في بعض المصنفات «إن عظام ابن آدم وعصبة من ماء الرجل،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r4.speaker: آخرون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r4.claim: Others explain the mixture as successive fetal stages from drop to clot to morsel and beyond.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r4.anchor: وقيل هو اختلاط أمر الجنين بالنقلة من النطفة إلى العلقة إلى المضغة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r5.speaker: آخرون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r5.claim: Another view says the mixture comprises blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r5.anchor: وقيل هو اختلاط الدم والبلغم والصفراء والسوداء فيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r6.claim: نبتليه means testing by bringing the human into existence and worldly life; it is a circumstantial phrase linked to the subject of خلقنا.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r6.anchor: ونبتليه معناه نختبره بالإيجاد والكون في الدنيا هو حال من الضمير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r7.claim: فجعلناه coordinates one complete clause with another complete clause.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r7.anchor: وقوله تعالى: فجعلناه عطف جملة تعم على جملة تعم،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r8.speaker: بعض النحويين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r8.claim: Some grammarians understand an implicit 'we tested him by making him hear and see'; here the test occurs through the senses, not compulsion, and نبتليه is not circumstantial.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r8.anchor: وقال بعض النحويين إنما المعنى فنبتليه جعلناه سميعا بصيرا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p428/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p428/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p428/r1.claim: The human here means the descendants of Adam, created from a mixed drop of fluid.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p428/r1.anchor: يعني ولد آدم من نطفة أمشاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p428/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p428/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p428/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba glosses “amshāj” as mixtures, the woman’s fluid mixed with the man’s.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p428/r2.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة أي أخلاط يقال مشجته فهو مشيج يريد اختلاط ماء المرأة بماء الرجل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p428/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p428/r3.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p428/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ treats “testing him” as fronted with the remainder delayed: God made him hearing and seeing in order to test him; al-Zajjāj gives the same purpose reading.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p428/r3.anchor: نبتليه قال الفراء هذا مقدم ومعناه التأخير لأن المعنى خلقناه وجعلناه سميعا بصيرا لنبتليه قال الزجاج المعنى جعلناه كذلك لنختبره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p285#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p285#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p285#2/r1.claim: Humanity came into existence after a time when it was not mentioned, reflecting insignificance and weakness; the mixed drop develops through stages and changing conditions.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p285#2/r1.anchor: أوجده بعد أن لم يكن شيئا يذكر (4) لحقارته وضعفه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p285#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p285#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p285#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the mixed drop consists of man’s fluid and woman’s fluid meeting; Ikrima, Mujahid, Hasan, and al-Rabi agree.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p285#2/r2.anchor: يعني: ماء الرجل وماء المرأة إذا اجتمعا واختلطا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p285#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p285#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p285#2/r3.claim: God tests the human, as in the statement that He tests which people are best in deeds.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p285#2/r3.anchor: نبتليه} أي: نختبره، كقوله: {ليبلوكم أيكم أحسن عملا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p285#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p285#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p285#2/r4.claim: God gave people hearing and sight through which they can obey or disobey.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p285#2/r4.anchor: جعلنا له سمعا وبصرا يتمكن بهما من الطاعة والمعصية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p666#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p666#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p666#2/r1.claim: Amshaj and mashaj are singular forms, like other lexical singulars, and can describe singular nutfah; amshaj is not a broken plural.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p666#2/r1.anchor: نطفة أمشاج } كبرمة أعشار ، وبرد أكياش : وهي ألفاظ مفردة غير جموع ، ولذلك وقعت صفات للأفراد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p666#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p666#2/r2.speaker: الشماخ
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p666#2/r2.claim: Al-Shammakh's verse uses mashaj for the mixed substance, illustrating the singular form.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p666#2/r2.anchor:
قال الشماخ :
طوت أحشاء مرتجة لوقت … على مشج سلالته مهين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p666#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p666#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p666#2/r3.claim: Mashaj and mazaj mean mixed; the drop consists of two fluids mingled together.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p666#2/r3.anchor: ومشجه ومزجه : بمعنى . والمعنى من نطفة قد امتزج لها الما آن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p666#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p666#2/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p666#2/r4.claim: Ibn Masud says amshaj refers to the veins in the semen.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p666#2/r4.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود : هي عروق النطفة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p666#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p666#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p666#2/r5.claim: Qatada says amshaj means varied colors and stages: first a drop, then a clot, then a morsel.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p666#2/r5.anchor: وعن قتادة : أمشاج ألوان وأطوار ، يريد : أنها تكون نطفة ، ثم علقة ، ثم مضغة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p666#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p666#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p666#2/r6.claim: Nabtali-hi is circumstantial: God created him intending to test him; alternatively it names his transfer from one state to another metaphorically as a trial.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p666#2/r6.anchor: نبتليه } في موضع الحال ، أي : خلقناه مبتلين له ، بمعنى : مريدين ابتلاءه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p666#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p666#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p666#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the testing as God's moving the fetus through stages in the womb, from a drop to a clot.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p666#2/r7.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : نصرفه في بطن أمه نطفة ثم علقة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p666#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p666#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p666#2/r8.claim: The proposal that nabtali-hi is temporally delayed, meaning God gave hearing and sight in order to test the person, is forced.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p666#2/r8.anchor: وقيل : هو في تقدير التأخير ، يعني : فجعلناه سميعا بصيرا لنبتليه ، وهو من التعسف

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r1.claim: He explains أمشاج as differing colors.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r1.anchor: أن الأمشاج الألوان , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r2.claim: He describes the man's seed as white and red and the woman's as green and yellow.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r2.anchor: مجاهد : نطفة الرجل بيضاء وحمراء , ونطفة المرأة خضراء وصفراء

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r3.speaker: قتادة عن أنس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r3.claim: Anas transmits a Prophetic report describing the man's fluid as thick and white, the woman's as thin and yellow, and saying resemblance follows whichever comes first or prevails.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r3.anchor: روى سعيد عن قتادة عن أنس قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( ماء الرجل غليظ أبيض , وماء المرأة رقيق أصفر

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r4.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r4.claim: He understands أمشاج as successive developmental stages from seed through clot, lump, bone, and flesh-covered bone.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r4.anchor: أن الأمشاج : الأطوار , وهو أن الخلق يكون طورا نطفة , وطورا علقة , وطورا مضغة , ثم طورا عظما , ثم يكسى العظم لحما , قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r5.claim: He explains أمشاج as veins in the seed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r5.anchor: أن الأمشاج العروق التي تكون في النطفة , قاله ابن مسعود

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r6.claim: نبتليه can mean that God tests the human being.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r7.claim: Alternatively, it means that God charges the human being with duties.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r8.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r8.claim: If the word means testing, one test is good and evil.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r9.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r9.claim: Another test is gratitude in prosperity and patience in adversity.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r9.anchor: نختبر شكره في السراء , وصبره في الضراء , قاله الحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r10.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r10.claim: If the word means assignment, it refers to work after creation.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r11.claim: Another view is that it means religion, which commands obedience and forbids sins.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r11.anchor: الدين ، ليكون مأمورا بالطاعة ، ومنهيا عن المعاصي

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r12.claim: Being made hearing and seeing may refer to the ears and eyes as a blessing, or to intellect and discernment that distinguish humans from animals.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r12.anchor: يسمع بالأذنين ويبصر بالعينين أمتنانا بالنعمة عليه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r13.speaker: الفراء ومقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r13.claim: They say the clause order is advanced: God made the human hearing and seeing in order to test him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r13.anchor: في الآية تقديم وتأخير أي فجعلناه سميعا بصيرا أن نبتليه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r14.speaker: ابن قتيبة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r14.claim: On the reordered reading, the test itself may occur through hearing and sight.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r14.anchor: لنبتليه بالسمع والبصر , قاله ابن قتيبة

MUJAHID:v2p711/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p711/r1.speaker: عكرمة
MUJAHID:v2p711/r1.claim: He explains أمشاج as the man's and woman's fluids mixed with one another.
MUJAHID:v2p711/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة قال ﴿ أمشاج ﴾ ماء الرجل وماء المرأة مشج أحدهما بالآخر

MUJAHID:v2p711/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p711/r2.speaker: الحسن
MUJAHID:v2p711/r2.claim: He says the man's fluid is mixed with the woman's and a creature is formed from them.
MUJAHID:v2p711/r2.anchor: عن الحسن قال يقول مشج ماء الرجل بماء المرأة فخلق منهن خلقا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#3/r1.claim: Al-insān may mean Adam's offspring, or specifically Adam; in the latter view, the period is his time in the womb until he became known among people.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#3/r1.anchor: ﴿ إنا خلقنا الإنسان ﴾ أي ولد آدم وقيل الأول ولد آدم أيضا وحين من الدهر على هذا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#3/r2.claim: Amshāj is an adjective or apposition describing a drop mixed from two fluids; it is a singular word, not a plural, despite its form.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#3/r2.anchor: ﴿ نطفة أمشاج ﴾ نعت أو بدل منها أي من نطفة قد امتزج فيها الماآن ومشجة ومزجة بمعنى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#3/r3.claim: Nabtali-hi is circumstantial: God created humanity intending to test it through commands and prohibitions.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#3/r3.anchor: ﴿ نبتليه ﴾ حال أي خلقناه مبتلين أي مريدين ابتلاءه بالأمر والنهي

NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#3/r4.claim: God made the human being hearing and seeing once these faculties came to be.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#3/r4.anchor: ﴿ فجعلناه سميعا بصيرا ﴾ ا ذا سمع وبصر

QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r1.claim: The verse links human creation to the account of forming humanity from clay in 23:12.
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r1.anchor: ولقد خلقنا الإنسان من سلالة من طين

QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r2.speaker: ابن السكيت
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r2.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit explains amshaj as mixtures blended from different kinds, resulting in diverse human temperaments.
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r2.anchor: وقال ابن السكيت: الأمشاج الأخلاط لأنها ممتزجة من أنواع

QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r3.speaker: أهل المعاني
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r3.claim: Grammarians say amshaj means gathered mixtures but is singular in sense as an adjective of the singular “drop.”
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r3.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: والأمشاج ما جمع وهو في معنى الواحد لأنه نعت للنطفة

QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r4.speaker: أبو أيوب الأنصاري
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r4.claim: Abu Ayyub al-Ansari transmits a report where a Jewish scholar asks the Prophet about male and female fluids and which one prevails to determine a child's sex.
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r4.anchor: وروي عن أبي أيوب الأنصاري: قال

QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r5.claim: “We test him” means God puts the person to a test or determines that testing will occur.
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r5.anchor: { نبتليه } أي نختبره. وقيل: نقدر فيه الابتلاء وهو الاختبار.

QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r6.speaker: الكلبي والحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r6.claim: Al-Kalbi says the test is good and evil; al-Hasan says it is gratitude in prosperity and patience in adversity.
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r6.anchor: أحدهما نختبره بالخير والشر قاله الكلبي: الثاني نختبر شكره في السراء وصبره في الضراء قاله الحسن.

QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r7.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r7.claim: Muqatil says the test involves deeds after creation; another view makes it religious responsibility, with commands and prohibitions.
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r7.anchor: أحدهما بالعمل بعد الخلق قاله مقاتل. الثاني بالدين ليكون مأمورا بالطاعة

QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says God transforms a human through successive stages of creation to test him with good and evil.
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r8.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس: «نبتليه»: نصرفه خلقا بعد خلق لنبتليه بالخير والشر.

QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r9.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r9.claim: Al-Farra reads making humans hearing and seeing as the purpose of testing, with forward-and-backward word order because testing follows complete creation.
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r9.anchor: وحكى محمد بن الجهم عن الفراء قال: المعنى والله أعلم { فجعلناه سميعا بصيرا } لنبتليه

QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r10.claim: Another interpretation says hearing and sight let people hear and see guidance.
QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r10.anchor: وقيل: { فجعلناه سميعا بصيرا }: يعني جعلنا له سمعا يسمع به الهدى

SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r1.claim: أمشاج modifies a singular نطفة in the plural because its meaning is collective, as in رفرف خضر, or because each element is treated as a drop.
SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r1.anchor: قوله: { أمشاج }: نعت ل " نطفة " ووقع الجمع صفة لمفرد؛ لأنه في معنى الجمع، كقوله تعالى:

SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r2.claim: He treats أمشاج as a singular lexical form such as برمة أعشار and برد أكياش, so plural form can describe a singular noun.
SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r2.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " أمشاج كبرمة أعشار، وبرد أكياش وهي ألفاظ مفردة غير جموع

SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r3.claim: He objects that this conflicts with Sibawayh and grammarians, who do not recognize أفعال as a singular pattern and reinterpret its singular uses.
SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r3.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وقوله مخالف لنص سيبويه والنحويين على أن أفعالا لا يكون مفردا.

SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r4.claim: The author defends al-Zamakhshari: he does not call أفعال singular, but says the adjective works by treating each fragment as a drop or piece.
SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r4.anchor: قلت: هو لم يجعل أفعالا مفردا، إنما قال: يوصف به المفرد، يعني بالتأويل الذي ذكرته

SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r5.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r5.claim: He says أمشاج means mixtures and gives مشج, مشج, or مشيج as singular forms.
SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r5.anchor: الأمشاج " الأخلاط، واحدها مشج بفتحتين، أو مشج كعدل وأعدال أو مشيج كشريف

SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r6.speaker: رؤبة
SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r6.claim: His verse uses أمشاج for mixed blood in an unformed embryo.
SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r6.anchor:
وقال رؤبة:
4434 يطرحن كل معجل نشاج
لم يكس جلدا من دم أمشاج

SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r7.speaker: الهذلي
SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r7.claim: His poetry uses مشيج for mixed material, describing feathers and arrow parts joined together.
SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r7.anchor:
وقال الهذلي:
4435 كأن الريش والفوقين منها
خلاف النصل سيط به مشيج

SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r8.claim: He denies that أمشاج is a plural of مشج, treating it instead as a singular form and saying the two fluids are mixed.
SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r8.anchor: وقد تقدم أن الزمخشري: منع ذلك.

SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r9.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r9.claim: He allows أمشاج as a plural of مشج, contrasting with al-Zamakhshari; the verb مشج means mix and مشيج or ممشوج mean mixed.
SAMIN-DURR:76:2/r9.anchor: فجوز أن يكون جمعا ل مشج كعدل، وقد تقدم أن الزمخشري: منع ذلك

SAMIN-DURR:76:2#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:76:2#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:76:2#2/r1.claim: نبتليه may be circumstantial for the creator, or for الإنسان since both clauses contain a pronoun returning to the one qualified.
SAMIN-DURR:76:2#2/r1.anchor: أحدهما: أنها حال من فاعل " خلقنا " ، أي: خلقنا حال كوننا مبتلين له.

SAMIN-DURR:76:2#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:76:2#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
SAMIN-DURR:76:2#2/r2.claim: If نبتليه means moving him through stages in the womb, its circumstantial sense is simultaneous with creation.
SAMIN-DURR:76:2#2/r2.anchor: مقارنة إن كان المعنى ب " نبتليه ": نصرفه في بطن أمه نطفة ثم علقة. وهو قول ابن عباس

SAMIN-DURR:76:2#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:76:2#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:76:2#2/r3.claim: If it means testing him through moral responsibility, the circumstantial sense is prospective because the newly created child is not yet accountable.
SAMIN-DURR:76:2#2/r3.anchor: وأن تكون مقدرة إن كان المعنى ب " نبتليه ": نختبره بالتكليف؛ لأنه وقت خلقه غير مكلف

SAMIN-DURR:76:2#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:76:2#2/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:76:2#2/r4.claim: He takes ابتلاء metaphorically as transferring a person from one condition to another; the author equates this with Ibn Abbas's interpretation.
SAMIN-DURR:76:2#2/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المراد: ناقلين له من حال إلى حال، فسمي ذلك ابتلاء على طريق الاستعارة

SAMIN-DURR:76:2#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:76:2#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:76:2#2/r5.claim: The proposed inversion, We made him hearing and seeing to test him, is unnecessary.
SAMIN-DURR:76:2#2/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم: " في الكلام تقديم وتأخير. والأصل: إنا جعلناه سميعا بصيرا نبتليه

RAZI-FULL:v30p209#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p209#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p209#2/r1.claim: Amshāj means mixtures; Ibn al-Aʿrābī gives the singulars mashaj and mashīj, and al-Kashshāf treats amshāj as a singular adjective, like words describing plural-like compositions.
RAZI-FULL:v30p209#2/r1.anchor: المشج : في اللغة الخلط ، يقال : مشج يمشج مشجا

RAZI-FULL:v30p209#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p209#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p209#2/r2.claim: Most commentators say the mixture is the man's and woman's fluids, linking it to 86:7; Ibn ʿAbbās describes the man's thick white fluid and woman's thin yellow one, assigning bones and strength to the man and flesh and blood to the woman.
RAZI-FULL:v30p209#2/r2.anchor: الأكثرون على أنه اختلاط نطفة الرجل بنطفة المرأة

RAZI-FULL:v30p209#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p209#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v30p209#2/r3.claim: Mujāhid explains the mixture as the different colors of the fluids: white from the man and yellow from the woman.
RAZI-FULL:v30p209#2/r3.anchor: قال مجاهد : هي ألوان النطفة فنطفة الرجل بيضاء ونطفة المرأة صفراء

RAZI-FULL:v30p209#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p209#2/r4.speaker: عبدالله
RAZI-FULL:v30p209#2/r4.claim: ʿAbd Allāh glosses amshāj as the veins within it.

RAZI-FULL:v30p209#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p209#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v30p209#2/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the fluid is mixed with menstrual blood, which is retained once pregnancy begins.
RAZI-FULL:v30p209#2/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن : يعني من نطفة مشجت بدم وهو دم الحيضة

RAZI-FULL:v30p209#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p209#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v30p209#2/r6.claim: Qatādah says water and blood mix first, then the substance becomes a clot and a lump; generally it changes from one state to another.
RAZI-FULL:v30p209#2/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة : الأمشاج هو أنه يختلط الماء والدم أولا ثم يصير علقة ثم يصير مضغة

RAZI-FULL:v30p209#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p209#2/r7.speaker: قوم
RAZI-FULL:v30p209#2/r7.claim: Some say the fluid contains the temperaments found in humans: heat, cold, moisture, and dryness, with “possessing mixtures” understood by ellipsis.
RAZI-FULL:v30p209#2/r7.anchor: وقال قوم : إن الله تعالى جعل في النطفة أخلاطا من الطبائع

RAZI-FULL:v30p209#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p209#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p209#2/r8.claim: Rāzī says the male-and-female-fluid explanation is best because once the fluid becomes a clot it is no longer called a nutfah; this does not rule out mixtures of earthly elements and air.
RAZI-FULL:v30p209#2/r8.anchor: قال بعض العلماء : الأولى هو أن المراد اختلاط نطفة الرجل والمرأة

RAZI-FULL:v30p210/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p210/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p210/r1.claim: Nabtali means “in order that We test him,” with omitted lām, as in ordinary expressions meaning “I came to pay you” or “to ask you for help.”
RAZI-FULL:v30p210/r1.anchor: نبتليه معناه لنبتليه ، وهو كقول الرجل : جئتك أقضي حقك ، أي لأقضي حقك

RAZI-FULL:v30p210/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p210/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p210/r2.claim: Nabtali is circumstantial: God created him while intending to test him.
RAZI-FULL:v30p210/r2.anchor: نبتليه في موضع الحال ، أي خلقناه مبتلين له ، يعني مريدين ابتلاءه

RAZI-FULL:v30p210/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p210/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p210/r3.claim: One reading rearranges the sequence: He made him hearing and seeing in order to test him.
RAZI-FULL:v30p210/r3.anchor: أن فيه تقديما وتأخيرا ، والمعنى { فجعلناه سميعا بصيرا } لنبتليه

RAZI-FULL:v30p210/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p210/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p210/r4.claim: Another reading needs no rearrangement: the human was created from mixed fluid for trial and examination, rather than for resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v30p210/r4.anchor: أنه لا حاجة إلى هذا التغيير ، والمعنى إنا خلقناه من هذه الأمشاج لا للبعث ، بل للابتلاء والامتحان

RAZI-FULL:v30p210/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p210/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p210/r5.claim: Hearing and sight may stand for understanding and discernment, obedience and knowledge, or the familiar senses; they are singled out as the greatest and noblest senses.
RAZI-FULL:v30p210/r5.anchor: والسمع والبصر كنايتان عن الفهم والتمييز

STUDYQURAN:76:2/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:76:2/r1.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:76:2/r1.claim: The mixed fluid refers to the combination of male and female fluids.
STUDYQURAN:76:2/r1.anchor: refers to the mixing of the male and female fluids (IK)

STUDYQURAN:76:2/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:76:2/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:76:2/r2.claim: The verse recalls the lowly physical origins of human beings.
STUDYQURAN:76:2/r2.anchor: verses that remind human beings of the base origins of their physical nature

STUDYQURAN:76:2/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:76:2/r3.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:76:2/r3.claim: The phrase about testing may instead begin a new sentence: “We will test him.”
STUDYQURAN:76:2/r3.anchor: That We may test him could also be read as a new sentence: “We will test him” (JJ)

STUDYQURAN:76:2/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:76:2/r4.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:76:2/r4.claim: Hearing and sight are gifts and part of the test, available for obedience or disobedience.
STUDYQURAN:76:2/r4.anchor: The gifts of hearing and sight are part of the test, as they may be used for obedience or disobedience (IK)

STUDYQURAN:76:2/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:76:2/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:76:2/r5.claim: The verse can indicate that the physical nature originating in mixed fluid is created to be tested.
STUDYQURAN:76:2/r5.anchor: the physical nature, that which comes from a drop of mixed fluid, is created for the purpose of being tested and tried

STUDYQURAN:76:2/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:76:2/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:76:2/r6.claim: For how human beings are tested, the commentary directs readers to 29:2–3 and 67:2.
STUDYQURAN:76:2/r6.anchor: Regarding the manner in which human beings are tested, see commentary on 29:2–3; 67:2.

TAB-FULL:v23p530#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p530#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p530#2/r2.claim: God created Adam's descendants from a small quantity of mixed male and female fluid; nuṭfah is any small amount of water in a vessel, from a cistern to a waterskin. Ibn Rawaha's verse illustrates nuṭfah.
TAB-FULL:v23p530#2/r2.anchor: من ماء الرجل وماء المرأة، والنطفة: كل ماء قليل في وعاء

TAB-FULL:v23p530#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p530#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p530#2/r3.claim: Amshaj means mixed fluids; its singular is mashj or mashij, and the verb mashaja means to mix. Ruʾbah's line witnesses the mixed-blood sense and Abu Dhuʾayb's the adjective mashij, mixed together.
TAB-FULL:v23p530#2/r3.anchor: وقوله: {أمشاج} [الإنسان: 2] يعني: أخلاط، واحدها: مشج ومشيج

TAB-FULL:v23p532/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p532/r1.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v23p532/r1.claim: Ikrima explains amshāj as the man’s and woman’s fluids mixing with one another.
TAB-FULL:v23p532/r1.anchor: عن سفيان، عن ابن الأصبهاني، عن عكرمة، {أمشاج نبتليه} [الإنسان: 2] قال: ماء الرجل وماء المرأة يمشج أحدهما بالآخر

TAB-FULL:v23p532/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p532/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p532/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the woman’s and man’s fluids mix.
TAB-FULL:v23p532/r2.anchor: عن عطية، عن ابن عباس، قال: ماء المرأة وماء الرجل يمشجان

TAB-FULL:v23p532/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p532/r3.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
