TAB-FULL:v23p532/r3.claim: Al-Rabīʿ b. Anas says the joined fluids of the man and woman are amshāj.
TAB-FULL:v23p532/r3.anchor: عن الربيع بن أنس، قال: إذا اجتمع ماء الرجل وماء المرأة فهو أمشاج

TAB-FULL:v23p532/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p532/r4.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v23p532/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan glosses amshāj as the woman’s fluid mixed with the man’s.
TAB-FULL:v23p532/r4.anchor: عن الحسن، قال: مشج ماء المرأة مع ماء الرجل

TAB-FULL:v23p532/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p532/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p532/r5.claim: Mujāhid says the child is created from the man’s and woman’s fluids, linking this to humanity’s creation from male and female.
TAB-FULL:v23p532/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: خلق الله الولد من ماء الرجل وماء المرأة، وقد قال الله: {يا أيها الناس إنا خلقناكم من ذكر وأنثى} [الحجرات: 13]

TAB-FULL:v23p532/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p532/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p532/r6.claim: Mujāhid describes the child as created from successive portions of the man’s and woman’s fluids.
TAB-FULL:v23p532/r6.anchor: عن أبي يحيى، عن مجاهد، قال: خلق من تارات ماء الرجل وماء المرأة

TAB-FULL:v23p532/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p532/r7.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v23p532/r7.claim: Other interpreters understand the mixed drop as undergoing successive forms: drop, clot, morsel, bones, then flesh.
TAB-FULL:v23p532/r7.anchor: وقال آخرون: أنما عني بذلك: إنا خلقنا الإنسان من نطفة ألوان ينتقل إليها، يكون نطفة، ثم يصير علقة، ثم مضغة، ثم عظما، ثم كسي لحما

TAB-FULL:v23p532/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p532/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p532/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the stages begin in earth and womb-fluid, then proceed through clot, morsel, bones, and a new creation.
TAB-FULL:v23p532/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {إنا خلقنا الإنسان من نطفة أمشاج نبتليه} [الإنسان: 2] الأمشاج خلق من ألوان، خلق من تراب، ثم من ماء الفرج والرحم

TAB-FULL:v23p532/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p532/r9.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v23p532/r9.claim: ʿIkrima also explains amshāj through the stages of drop, clot, morsel, and bones.
TAB-FULL:v23p532/r9.anchor: عن عكرمة، في هذه الآية {أمشاج} [الإنسان: 2] قال: نطفة، ثم علقة، ثم مضغة، ثم عظما

TAB-FULL:v23p534/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p534/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p534/r1.claim: Qatāda describes successive creation stages from drop to bones, which God clothes with flesh before creating the human anew and growing hair.
TAB-FULL:v23p534/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {إنا خلقنا الإنسان من نطفة أمشاج} [الإنسان: 2] أطوار الخلق، طورا نطفة، وطورا علقة، وطورا مضغة، وطورا عظاما

TAB-FULL:v23p534/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p534/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p534/r2.claim: Qatāda also glosses amshāj as water and blood mixed, followed by a clot and then a morsel.
TAB-FULL:v23p534/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {أمشاج نبتليه} [الإنسان: 2] قال: الأمشاج: اختلط الماء والدم، ثم كان علقة، ثم كان مضغة

TAB-FULL:v23p534/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p534/r3.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v23p534/r3.claim: Other interpreters say amshāj refers to the varying colors of the drop.
TAB-FULL:v23p534/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون: عني بذلك اختلاف ألوان النطفة

TAB-FULL:v23p534/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p534/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p534/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses amshāj as differing colors.
TAB-FULL:v23p534/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {أمشاج نبتليه} [الإنسان: 2] يقول: مختلفة الألوان

TAB-FULL:v23p534/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p534/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p534/r5.claim: Mujāhid explains the term as the colors of the drop.

TAB-FULL:v23p534/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p534/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p534/r6.claim: Mujāhid says whichever of the two fluids precedes determines resemblance to the paternal and maternal uncles.
TAB-FULL:v23p534/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: أي الماءين سبق أشبه عليه أعمامه وأخواله

TAB-FULL:v23p534/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p534/r7.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p534/r7.claim: Mujāhid specifies the man’s fluid as white and red and the woman’s as red and green.
TAB-FULL:v23p534/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد، {أمشاج نبتليه} [الإنسان: 2] قال: ألوان النطفة؛ نطفة الرجل بيضاء وحمراء، ونطفة المرأة حمراء وخضراء

TAB-FULL:v23p534/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p534/r8.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v23p534/r8.claim: Other interpreters say the mixed elements are the veins inside the drop.
TAB-FULL:v23p534/r8.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل هي العروق التي تكون في النطفة

TAB-FULL:v23p534/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p534/r9.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v23p534/r9.claim: ʿAbd Allāh explains the drop’s amshāj as its veins.
TAB-FULL:v23p534/r9.anchor: عن عبد الله، قال: أمشاجها: عروقها

TAB-FULL:v23p534/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p534/r10.speaker: أبوه
TAB-FULL:v23p534/r10.claim: Usāma b. Zayd’s father says amshāj are the veins within the drop.
TAB-FULL:v23p534/r10.anchor: عن أبيه، قال: هي العروق التي تكون في النطفة

TAB-FULL:v23p534/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p534/r11.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p534/r11.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the mixture of male and female fluids: the verse still calls it a drop, whereas after becoming a clot it is no longer a drop.
TAB-FULL:v23p534/r11.anchor: وأشبه هذه الأقوال بالصواب قول من قال: معنى ذلك {من نطفة أمشاج} [الإنسان: 2] نطفة الرجل ونطفة المرأة، لأن الله وصف النطفة بأنها أمشاج

TAB-FULL:v23p534/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p534/r12.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p534/r12.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rejects differing male-fluid colors as the intended meaning, since the known fluid is a single color; he suspects the veins view aimed at that meaning.
TAB-FULL:v23p534/r12.anchor: وأما الذين قالوا: إن نطفة الرجل بيضاء وحمراء، فإن المعروف من نطفة الرجل أنها سحراء على لون واحد، وهي بيضاء تضرب إلى الحمرة

TAB-FULL:v23p537/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p537/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p537/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī glosses nbtalīhi as We test him.
TAB-FULL:v23p537/r1.anchor: فأما الابتلاء فبالخلق مع صحة الفطرة، وسلامة العقل من الآفة

TAB-FULL:v23p537/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p537/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p537/r2.claim: Some Arabic grammarians treat giving hearing and sight as the means of testing; al-Ṭabarī rejects the inversion, saying trial is by sound nature and an unimpaired mind.
TAB-FULL:v23p537/r2.anchor: فأما الابتلاء فبالخلق مع صحة الفطرة، وسلامة العقل من الآفة

TAB-FULL:v23p537/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p537/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p537/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rejects that parsing: testing occurs through sound faculties and an intact mind, even if hearing or sight is absent; those faculties instead recall divine favors and the need for gratitude.
TAB-FULL:v23p537/r3.anchor: وإن عدم السمع والبصر. وأما إخباره إيانا أنه جعل لنا أسماعا وأبصارا في هذه الآية، فتذكير منه لنا بنعمه

TAB-FULL:v23p537/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p537/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p537/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the test is creation with sound nature and an unimpaired mind, linking humanity’s purpose to worshipping God.
TAB-FULL:v23p537/r4.anchor: كما قال : {وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون} [الذاريات: 56]

TABATABAI:76:2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:76:2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:76:2/r1.claim: The sura describes human creation and guidance to gratitude or disbelief, then punishment and the blessings of the righteous at length; it closes by telling the Prophet to remain patient and worship.
TABATABAI:76:2/r1.anchor: تذكر السورة خلق الإنسان بعد ما لم يكن شيئا مذكورا ثم هدايته السبيل إما شاكرا وإما كفورا وأن الله إعتد للكافرين أنواع العذاب

TABATABAI:76:2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:76:2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:76:2/r2.claim: The sura is considered wholly Medinan or partly Medinan with its final nine verses Meccan; Ahl al-Bayt reports uniformly and Sunni reports extensively call it Medinan, while another view calls it wholly Meccan.
TABATABAI:76:2/r2.anchor: وهي اثنتان وعشرون آية من أولها

TABATABAI:76:2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:76:2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:76:2/r3.claim: The opening question expects affirmation: a period did pass; early exegetes who glossed هل as قد meant this force, not a separate dictionary sense of هل.
TABATABAI:76:2/r3.anchor: الاستفهام للتقرير فيفيد ثبوت معنى الجملة وتحققه أي قد أتى على الانسان

TABATABAI:76:2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:76:2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:76:2/r4.claim: Human means the human species, not Adam, because the following verse says humanity was created from a sperm-drop.
TABATABAI:76:2/r4.anchor: والمراد بالإنسان الجنس. وأما قول بعضهم إن المراد به آدم عليه السلام فلا يلائمه قوله في الآية التالية

TABATABAI:76:2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:76:2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:76:2/r5.claim: A hin is any bounded portion of time, short or long, whereas dahr is an expanse of time without specified beginning or end.
TABATABAI:76:2/r5.anchor: والحين قطعة من الزمان محدودة قصيرة كانت أو طويلة، والدهر الزمان الممتد من دون تحديد ببداية أو نهاية.

TABATABAI:76:2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:76:2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:76:2/r6.claim: Being mentioned means being counted among existing things such as earth and sea; the verse denies that humans then existed as an actual named being, not that their material basis existed.
TABATABAI:76:2/r6.anchor: أي شيئا يذكر باسمه في المذكورات أي كان يذكر مثلا الأرض والسماء والبر والبحر وغير ذلك ولا يذكر الإنسان لأنه لم يوجد بعد

TABATABAI:76:2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:76:2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:76:2/r7.claim: The passage argues that humans are originated and need a maker, who equipped them with hearing and sight to recognize the true way and reach either lasting bliss or painful punishment.
TABATABAI:76:2/r7.anchor: والآية وما يتلوها من الآيات واقعة في سياق الاحتجاج يبين بها أن الانسان حادث يحتاج في وجوده إلى صانع يصنعه وخالق يخلقه

TABATABAI:76:2-3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:76:2-3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:76:2-3/r1.claim: Nutfah originally means a little water, then came to mean the male animal fluid from which a like creature develops; amshaj means mixed, describing its diverse elements or the mixing of male and female fluids.
TABATABAI:76:2-3/r1.anchor: النطفة في الأصل بمعنى الماء القليل غلب استعماله في ماء الذكور من الحيوان الذي يتكون منه مثله، وأمشاج جمع مشيج

TABATABAI:76:2-3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:76:2-3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:76:2-3/r2.claim: God's testing by creation means moving the embryo through successive stages, as elsewhere described, until it becomes a new creation.
TABATABAI:76:2-3/r2.anchor: والابتلاء نقل الشيء من حال إلى حال ومن طور إلى طور كابتلاء الذهب في البوتقة، وابتلاؤه تعالى الإنسان في خلقه

TABATABAI:76:2-3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:76:2-3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:76:2-3/r3.claim: The alternative says testing means imposing religious duties; the next clause makes hearing and sight result from the test, whereas they should enable a test. Reordering the clauses to rescue this view is unconvincing.
TABATABAI:76:2-3/r3.anchor: على الابتلاء ولو كان المراد به التكليف كان من الواجب تفريعه على جعله سميعا بصيرا

TABATABAI:76:2-3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:76:2-3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:76:2-3/r4.claim: Hearing and sight equip human beings to receive God's call through prophets and books and to see signs of the origin and return, guiding them to faith and good works or punishment.
TABATABAI:76:2-3/r4.anchor: جعله سميعا بصيرا للتوسل به في التدبير الربوبي إلى غايته وهي أن يرى آيات الله الدالة على المبدإ والمعاد ويسمع

TABATABAI:76:2-3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:76:2-3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:76:2-3/r5.claim: Naming humanity instead of using a pronoun records that God created humans and directs their affairs.
TABATABAI:76:2-3/r5.anchor: وذكر الإنسان في الآية من وضع الظاهر موضع الضمير والنكتة فيه تسجيل أنه تعالى هو خالقه ومدبر أمره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r1.claim: Mashj means a mixture; amshāj is the plural of mashj, and a mixed thing is also called mashīj or mamshūj.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r1.anchor: المشج في اللغة: "الخلط، يقال: مشج (يمشج) (¬7) مشجا إذا خلط، والأمشاج: الأخلاط

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r2.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r2.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī gives mashj and mashaj as singular forms and cites al-Shammākh and another verse as evidence for the word.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r2.anchor: قال ابن الأعرابي: واحدها: مشج، ومشج، وأنشد (قول الشماخ

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r3.speaker: الشمّاخ
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r3.claim: Al-Shammākh’s line uses mashj to witness the lexical sense of a mixed substance.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة والفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r4.claim: Abū ʿUbayda and al-Farrāʾ define amshāj as mixtures and compare mashīj to a mixture or blended thing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r4.anchor: وقال [أبو عبيدة (¬4)] (¬5)، والفراء (¬6): الأمشاج: الأخلاط، ويقال للشيء إذا خلط: مشيج، كقولك: خليط

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r5.speaker: هذلي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r5.claim: A Hudhalī poet compares a blood-stained arrow to something mixed, as evidence for mashīj.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r6.claim: Although nutfah is singular, it is described with plural amshāj, like a pot made up of fragments, a worn garment, or scattered land.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r6.anchor: ووصف (النطفة) وهي واحدة بالأمشاج، وهي جمع، كوصف: البرمة (¬2) بالأعشار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r7.speaker: أهل اللغة والمفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r7.claim: All lexicographers and commentators agree that amshāj means mixtures.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r7.anchor: ومعنى أمشاج: أخلاط في قول جميع أهل اللغة (¬5)، # (والمفسرين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r8.speaker: ابن عباس والكلبي ومقاتل وعكرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r8.claim: The majority, including Ibn ʿAbbās in ʿAṭāʾ’s report, al-Kalbī, Muqātil, and ʿIkrima, say the male and female fluids mix; they assign bone, sinew, and strength to the man and flesh, blood, and hair to the woman.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r8.anchor: أنه اختلاط نطفة الرجل بنطفة المرأة، وهو قول ابن عباس (¬4) في رواية عطاء، (والكلبي) (¬5) (¬6)، ومقاتل (¬7)، # (وعكرمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r9.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r9.claim: Mujāhid says the mixture is the fluids’ colors: the man’s is white and red, the woman’s green and red; al-Kalbī and al-Walībī’s Ibn ʿAbbās report also transmit this view.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r9.anchor: مجاهد: هي ألوان النطفة، نطفة الرجل بيضاء، وحمراء، ونطفة المرأة خضراء، وحمراء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r10.speaker: عبد الله
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r10.claim: ʿAbd Allāh says the mixture is the veins formed in the semen.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r10.anchor: عبد الله: أمشاجها عروقها (¬7). يعني: العروق التي تكون في النطفة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r11.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r11.claim: Al-Ḥasan says it is a drop mixed with menstrual blood, which mingles with the conception after pregnancy stops the woman’s menstruation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p9/r11.anchor: الحسن: يعني من نطفة مشجت بدم، وهو دم الحيضة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p14/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p14/r1.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p14/r1.claim: Qatāda says water and blood mix, then the embryo becomes a clot and then a morsel of flesh; a report from ʿIkrima is similar and al-Zajjāj selects it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p14/r1.anchor: قتادة: الأمشاج إذا اختلط الماء والدم، ثم كان علقة، ثم كان مضغة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p14/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p14/r2.speaker: سماك عن عكرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p14/r2.claim: Sammāk’s report from ʿIkrima gives a similar account of the mixture.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p14/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p14/r3.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p14/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj chooses the interpretation of mixtures of semen and blood, followed by movement from one state to another.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p14/r3.anchor: الزجاج فقال: أمشاج: أخلاط من مني ودم، ثم ينقل من حال إلى حال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p14/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p14/r4.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p14/r4.claim: The language scholars say God placed mixed temperaments in the semen, including heat, cold, dryness, and moisture, then proportioned them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p14/r4.anchor: أهل المعاني: إن الله جعل في النطفة أخلاطا من الطبائع التي تكون في الإنسان من الحرارة، والبرودة، واليبوسة، والرطوبة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p14/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p14/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p14/r5.claim: The phrase means a semen possessing mixtures, with the construct noun omitted.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p14/r5.anchor: والتقدير: من نطفة ذات أمشاج، فحذف المضاف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p14/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p14/r6.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p14/r6.claim: Muqātil says God made the person able to hear and see after the semen in order to test him through deeds.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p14/r6.anchor: فجعلناه بعد النطفة سميعا بصيرا لنبتليه بالعمل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p14/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p14/r7.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p14/r7.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the order is semantically reversed: God created him, made him hearing and seeing, in order to test him; al-Zajjāj and Ibn Qutayba agree.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p14/r7.anchor: الفراء: المعنى: جعلناه سميعا بصيرا لنبتليه، فهي مقدمة معناها التأخير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p14/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p14/r8.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p14/r8.claim: Another analysis attaches testing to the initial creation, as its circumstantial purpose, then says hearing and sight equip a person for the test.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p14/r8.anchor: خلقناه من نطفة أمشاج لنبتليه، لنختبره في الاعتبار بهذه الأحوال في خلقه

ASAD-NOTES:76:1#n3/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:76:1#n3/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:76:1#n3/r1.claim: Asad supplies “with the female ovum” as the unstated counterpart in the description of the mixed drop.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p296/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p296/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p296/r1.claim: The surah follows the human through nonexistence, embryonic formation, moral responsibility, and the afterlife, making its title The Human apt.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p296/r1.anchor: السورة كلها تذكّره في كل مراحل الإنسان فهي بحق سورة الإنسان

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p296/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p296/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p296/r2.claim: هل أتى is an interrogative of confirmation, not a factual report: the human answers yes, prompting the question who created him from nothing, answered by إنا خلقنا.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p296/r2.anchor: فالله تعالى يسأل هل أتى على الإنسان فيجيب الإنسان نعم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p301/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p301/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p301/r1.claim: أمشاج means mixtures and can function as singular or plural, like بشر, الفلك, and طفل in Arabic usage.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p301/r1.anchor: الأمشاج هي الأخلاط وكما قلنا تستعمل للمفرد والجمع

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p301/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p301/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p301/r2.claim: The plural أمشاج is chosen over مشيجة or مشج to stress the many mixtures and interminglings in the drop; Arabic also pluralizes وصف for extensive distribution, as in سباسب and قفار.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p301/r2.anchor: اختيار الجمع لكثرة ما فيها من أخلاط وامتزاجات

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p302/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p302/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p302/r1.claim: نبتليه means test; the افتعل form is more emphatic than بلى يبلو, as in صبر/اصطبر and كسب/اكتسب, and Quranic uses include the tests after Uhud and the Confederates.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p302/r1.anchor: الفعل المجرد بلى يبلو أما فعل ابتلى يبتلي ففيه مبالغة أكثر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p302/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p302/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p302/r2.claim: The rule that more letters always add meaning is not universal: حذر, a form of intensive expression, is stronger than حاذر.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p302/r2.anchor: القول أن الزيادة في المبنى تفيد الزيادة في المعنى غير مضطرد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p302/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p302/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p302/r3.claim: The author raises why al-Mulk uses the lighter يبلوكم rather than يبتليكم and asks how the two forms differ.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p302/r3.anchor: لماذا جاء التخفيف في البلاء ولم يستعمل ليبتليكم؟

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p303/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p303/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p303/r1.claim: Al-Mulk ends by calling God الغفور; the lighter يبلو form suits forgiveness, since intensified trial and severity do not suit the forgiving quality and easing is part of forgiveness.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p303/r1.anchor: المغفرة تقتضي التخفيف أولاً لأن الابتلاء والشدّة لا تتناسبان مع الغفور

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p303/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p303/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p303/r2.claim: Human names hearing, sight, and guidance as means of testing, so نبتليه fits its fuller account; al-Mulk omits those means and moves to the heavens, suiting يبلوكم.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p303/r2.anchor: فلما أطال في ذكر ما تردد أطال في صيغة الإبتلاء

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p304/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p304/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p304/r1.claim: Human details tested actions, including vows, feeding the needy, patience, worship, and the outcomes of believers and wrongdoers; al-Mulk gives less detail, making the intensified form apt to this surah's context.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p304/r1.anchor: السياق والوسائل وما ذكر من الأعمال جعل ذكر الابتلاء أنسب من كل ناحية

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p304/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p304/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p304/r2.claim: One grammatical reading makes نبتليه a purpose clause meaning لنبتليه, like لنبلوكم in al-Mulk.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p304/r2.anchor: التعليل نبتليه بمعنى لنبتليه كما قال في سورة الملك لنبلوكم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p305/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p305/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p305/r1.claim: A second reading treats نبتليه as a future circumstantial clause, either of the subject (God testing him) or object (the human created to be tested); an estimated state can occur later than the main action, unlike a simultaneous or narrated-past state.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p305/r1.anchor: أن تكون حال مقدرة من الفاعل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p305/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p305/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p305/r2.claim: The unprefixed نبتليه deliberately allows purpose and future circumstantial readings from either subject or object; لنبتليه would express purpose alone.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p305/r2.anchor: لما أفاد إلا معنى التعليل فقط

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p306/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p306/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p306/r1.claim: Al-Mulk cannot use this circumstantial construction because it mentions creation of death and life without naming the human; the Human surah names him and permits the broader meaning.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p306/r1.anchor: فكيف تأتي الحال وهو لم يذكر الإنسان

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p306/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p306/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p306/r2.claim: The passage names every condition of testing: God and the human, hearing, sight, reason, choice and its paths, the two responses, and their outcomes in Paradise or Hell.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p306/r2.anchor: لم يدع شيئاً يخص الابتلاء إلا وذكره في هذه الآية

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p306/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p306/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p306/r3.claim: Hearing precedes sight because hearing is more important for moral obligation: a deaf person is harder to instruct than a blind person.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p306/r3.anchor: السمع أهم في باب التكليف والاختبار من البصر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p307/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p307/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p307/r1.claim: Hearing and sight precede guidance because they convey information to the mind and usually enable understanding of guidance and rulings.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p307/r1.anchor: السمع والبصر يوصلان المعلومات إلى العقل وبدونهما تتعسّر الهداية

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p307/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p307/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p307/r2.claim: The two descriptions are joined without و so readers do not infer that God created one group who hears and another group who sees.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p307/r2.anchor: لئلا يُفهم أنه تعالى خلق الإنسان على نوعين منهم من يسمع ومنهم من يُبصر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p307/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p307/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p307/r3.claim: The author asks why the verse uses the intensive form سميع rather than سمّاع, setting up the following discussion.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p307/r3.anchor: لماذا استخدم صيغة المبالغة (سميعاً) ولم يستخدم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p308/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p308/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p308/r1.claim: In Quranic usage سميع describes God and humans in praise, while سمّاع describes humans only in blame; since this verse bestows hearing as a favor, سميع is the fitting form.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p308/r1.anchor: صيغة المبالغة سميع تستعمل في مقام المدح والامتنان والتفضّل بالنعمة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p309/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p309/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p309/r1.claim: إنا هديناه echoes إنا خلقنا with emphatic divine attribution because guidance is crucial, perhaps exceeding creation; if creation for worship is emphasized, guidance must be emphasized too.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p309/r1.anchor: إذا كان الخلق مؤكد فلا بد من أن تكون الهداية مؤكدة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p345/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p345/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p345/r1.claim: Three emphasis markers in the revelation verse name sender, message, and recipient; greater emphasis is warranted because Quraysh strongly denied revelation but did not deny God as creator, and revelation, the worship-giving book, is creation's purpose.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p345/r1.anchor: فالتوكيد إذن يعتمد على شدة إنكار الشخص للأمر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p355/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p355/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p355/r3.claim: The author asks why this verse says نحن خلقناهم while the opening says إنا خلقنا الإنسان, leaving the wording contrast open here.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p355/r3.anchor: في أول السورة قال تعالى (إنا خلقنا الإنسان من نطفة أمشاج) وفي هذه الآية قال تعالى (نحن خلقناهم) فلماذا التوكيد بـ (إن) في الأولى

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p336#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p336#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p336#2/r1.claim: Qatada explains the mixed fluid as water and blood joined together, then becoming a clot and then a lump of flesh.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p336#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ أمشاج نبتليه ﴾ قال الأمشاج إذا اختلط الماء والدم ثم كان علقة ثم كان مضغة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r2.claim: الإنسان means humankind, since Adam was not created from a mixed drop.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r2.anchor: إنا خلقنا الإنسان: هو جنس بني آدم لأن آدم لم يخلق من نطفة أمشاج

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r3.claim: أمشاج means mixtures and describes the drop.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود، أسامة بن زيد عن أبيه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r4.claim: They explain the mixture as the veins in the reproductive fluid.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r4.anchor: فقال ابن مسعود وأسامة بن زيد عن أبيه: هي العروق التي في النطفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r5.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، الربيع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r5.claim: They say the male and female fluids mix in the womb and the human is created from both.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس ومجاهد والربيع: هو ماء الرجل وماء المرأة اختلطا في الرحم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r6.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r6.claim: He says the sperm mixes with menstrual blood, which ceases when pregnancy begins.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r6.anchor: وقال الحسن: اختلاط النطفة بدم الحيض، فإذا حبلت ارتفع الحيض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r7.speaker: ابن عباس، عكرمة، قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r7.claim: They take the mixed stages as transitions from a drop to a clot, a morsel, and further stages until human formation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r7.anchor: أمشاج منتقلة من نطفة إلى علقة إلى مضغة إلى غير ذلك إلى إنشائه إنسانا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r8.speaker: ابن عباس، الكلبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r8.claim: They say the mixture refers to the different colors of the reproductive fluid.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا والكلبي: هي ألوان النطفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r9.claim: Another view identifies mixtures of blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile; the singular noun can be generic with a plural adjective, or each part can be treated as a drop.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r9.anchor:
وقيل:
أخلاط الدم والبلغم والصفراء والسوداء، والنطفة أريد بها الجنس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r10.claim: He says أمشاج is an individually inflected form, like برمة أعشار and برد أكياس, so it can qualify a singular noun; نطفة مشج is also said.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r10.anchor:
وقال الزمخشري:
نطفة أمشاج، كبرمة أعسار، وبرد أكياس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r11.claim: Abu Hayyan says this contradicts Sibawayh and the grammarians: أفعال is not singular, so apparent singular adjectives of this pattern require interpretation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r11.anchor: وقوله مخالف لنص سيبويه والنحويين على أن أفعالا لا يكون مفردا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r12.claim: نبتليه means testing the human with religious obligation in worldly life; on this reading the circumstantial clause is prospective.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r13.claim: Another explanation from Ibn Abbas is that God carries the embryo through its stages in the womb; then the circumstantial state accompanies creation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r13.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: نصرفه في بطن أمه نطفة ثم علقة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r14.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r14.claim: He calls the transfer from one state to another ‘testing’ metaphorically; Abu Hayyan says this is Ibn Abbas's sense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r14.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ويجوز أن يراد ناقلين له من حال إلى حال فسمي ذلك الابتلاء على طريق الاستعارة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r15.claim: Other readings take testing as bringing the human into existence and worldly life, with a circumstantial clause accompanying creation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r15.anchor:
وقيل:
نبتليه بالإيجاد والكون في الدنيا، فهي حال مقارنة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r16.claim: A proposed word order reversal makes granting hearing and sight the test; Abu Hayyan says there is no need to posit inversion because the ordinary order already makes sense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r16.anchor: وقيل: في الكلام تقديم وتأخير الأصل. فجعلناه سميعا بصيرا نبتليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r17.claim: God's gift of hearing and sight is also a gift of discernment and understanding, since these faculties enable them and are the noblest senses for apprehending great objects.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p358/r17.anchor: وامتن تعالى عليه بجعله بهاتين الصفتين، وهما كناية عن التمييز والفهم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p151/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p151/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p151/r1.claim: Repeating “the human” rather than using a pronoun emphasizes the material involved; because the verse says humanity came from a drop, it primarily means human descendants rather than Adam, or it uses the majority's material for the whole class.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p151/r1.anchor: وفي إقامة الظاهر مقام المضمر فضل التقرير والتمكين في النفس

ALUSI-FULL:v29p151/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p151/r2.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p151/r2.claim: Reports from Qatada, al-Thawri, Ikrima, al-Shaʿbi, and Ibn Abbas say Adam is intended; Ibn Abbas says he lay between Mecca and Taif for forty years before receiving the spirit.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p151/r2.anchor: ورويت إرادته عن قتادة والثوري وعكرمة والشعبي وابن عباس أيضا وقال في رواية أبي صالح عنه مرت به أربعون سنة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p151/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p151/r3.speaker: الضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v29p151/r3.claim: In another report from Ibn Abbas through al-Dahhak, Adam was formed in stages: clay, dark mud, then molded clay, forty years each, and his form was complete after 120 years before the spirit was breathed into him.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p151/r3.anchor: وفي رواية الضحاك عنه أنه خلق من طين فأقام أربعين سنة ثم من حمأ مسنون

ALUSI-FULL:v29p151/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p151/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v29p151/r4.claim: Al-Mawardi reports Ibn Abbas's view that the “time” was an extended period whose length is unknown; Ikrima similarly says no one knows how long passed before God created the human.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p151/r4.anchor: وحكي الماوردي عنه أن الحين المذكور ههنا هو الزمن الطويل الممتد الذي لا يعرف مقداره

ALUSI-FULL:v29p151/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p151/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p151/r5.claim: Some Sufis construe the opening question as denying any time when humans were not mentioned, implying the human species has existed for every time; Alusi calls this species-level eternity disbelief by consensus.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p151/r5.anchor: وظاهره القول بقدم الإنسان في الزمان على معنى أنه لم يكن زمان إلا وفيه إنسان

ALUSI-FULL:v29p151/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p151/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p151/r6.claim: An attempted defense says Ibn Arabi meant humanity's eternal archetype, not temporal existence: the Perfect Human makes divine knowledge visible when clothed in existence; Alusi counters that all things in immutable archetypes are eternal, not humanity alone.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p151/r6.anchor: لو لم يكن في العالم من هو على صورة الحق ما حصل المقصود من العلم بالحق

ALUSI-FULL:v29p151/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p151/r7.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
ALUSI-FULL:v29p151/r7.claim: Alusi says leading Companions understood the verse affirmatively: Umar heard it recited and wished the phrase had been completed, showing he took it as a report of prior nonexistence.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p151/r7.anchor: أخرج عبد بن حميد وغيره عن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه سمع رجلا يقرأ هل أتى

ALUSI-FULL:v29p151/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p151/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v29p151/r8.claim: Ibn Masud likewise wished the verse completed; after he was rebuked, he picked up a clod and said he wished he were like it.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p151/r8.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه سمع رجلا يتلو ذلك فقال يا ليتها تمت

ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r1.claim: Amshaj is parsed as a plural of several related forms meaning mixtures; its plural adjective modifies the singular drop because it contains multiple fluids or constituent parts and qualities.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r1.anchor: بالجمع وهي مفردة لأن بها مجموع ماء الرجل والمرأة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r2.claim: A report distinguishes bodily contributions: male fluid contributes sinew, bone, and strength, while female fluid contributes flesh and blood.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r2.anchor: وفي بعض الآثار إنما كان من عصب وعظم وقوة فمن ماء الرجل وما كان من لحم ودم فمن ماء المرأة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari prefers treating amshaj as a singular pattern on afʿāl; the usual position of Sibawayh and most grammarians is that this pattern is not singular.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r3.anchor: واختاره الزمخشري والمشهور عن نص سيبويه وجمهور النحاة أن أفعالا لا يكون جمعا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r4.claim: Most interpreters take the mixed drop to combine male and female fluids; another view mixes blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile, while a third treats amshaj itself as those four humors.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r4.anchor: نطفة مختلطة عند الأكثرين نطفة اختلط وامتزج فيها الماءان وقيل اختلط فيها الدم والبلغم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r5.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r5.claim: Mujahid says the drop has colors: male fluid is white, female fluid yellow, and after mixing and remaining in the womb it turns green, like water left to stand.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r5.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر عن مجاهد أنه قال أمشاج أي ألوان أي ذات ألوان

ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r6.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r6.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam interprets amshaj as the veins in the drop, an explanation also transmitted from Ibn Masud.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r6.anchor: أخرج عن زيد بن أسلم أنه قال الأمشاج العروق التي في النطفة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r7.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r7.claim: Ikrima and Ibn Abbas interpret the mixtures as developmental stages from drop to clot to morsel through complete formation and the breathing of the spirit.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r7.anchor: وروي عكرمة وكذاابن عباس أنه قال أمشاج أطوار أي ذات أطوار

ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r8.claim: “Testing him” is a prospective circumstantial clause describing God's intention to test the human through later accountability, or figuratively the transfer from stage to stage, which answers why testing precedes becoming hearing and seeing.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r8.anchor: وقوله تعالى نبتليه حال من فاعل خلقنا والمراد مريدين ابتلاءه واختباره بالتكليف فيما بعد

ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r9.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r9.claim: Al-Farraʾ proposes fronting the clause: God made the human hearing and seeing in order to test him; Alusi calls this forced because the syntax and sense do not support the reversal.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r9.anchor: وقيل الكلام على التقديم والتأخير والجملة استئناف تعليلي أي فجعلناه سميعا بصيرا لنبتليه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r10.claim: Making the human hearing and seeing follows from the test's purpose: these faculties let him perceive signs in the world, himself, and revelation.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p152/r10.anchor: وهذا الجعل كالمسبب عن الابتلاء لأن المقصود من جعله كذلك أن ينظر الآيات الآفاقية والأنفسية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p292#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p292#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p292#2/r1.claim: Nabtali means God tests the human through commands and prohibitions.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p292#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p292#2/r2.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p292#2/r2.claim: Some Arab grammarians propose a reordered syntax: God made the human hearing and seeing in order to test him, since testing follows completion of creation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p292#2/r2.anchor: قال بعض أهل العربية: فيه تقديم وتأخير، مجازه فجعلناه سميعا بصيرا لنبتليه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p260#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p260#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p260#2/r1.claim: Human beings began as nothing, then God moved them through reproductive stages; reflecting on this should expose their frailty and the folly of rejecting resurrection and divine favor.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p260#2/r1.anchor: قد كان لا شيء فلا نطفة ولا علقة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p260#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p260#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p260#2/r2.claim: The noun ‘human’ generalizes to Adam and all his descendants, while the account then specifies the descendants’ creation from a small amount of male and female fluid.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p260#2/r2.anchor: وأظهر ولم يضمر لأن الثاني خاص والأول عام لآدم عليه الصلاة والسلام وجميع ولده

BIQAI-FULL:v8p260#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p260#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p260#2/r3.claim: A nuṭfah is a small quantity of fluid in a container and the material carrying generative power; the author attributes different physical contributions to male and female fluids and says resemblance follows whichever fluid prevails.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p260#2/r3.anchor: وما كان من عصب وعظم فمن نظفة الرجل , وما كان من دم ولحم وشعر فمن ماء المرأة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p260#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p260#2/r4.speaker: يماني
BIQAI-FULL:v8p260#2/r4.claim: Yamānī explains amshāj as any two colors mixed together.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p260#2/r4.anchor: وقال يمان : كل لونين اختلطا فهو أمشاج

BIQAI-FULL:v8p260#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p260#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
BIQAI-FULL:v8p260#2/r5.claim: Qatāda explains amshāj as the successive stages of creation, beginning with the drop and continuing afterward.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p260#2/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة : هي أطوار الخلق من النطفة وما بعدهما

BIQAI-FULL:v8p260#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p260#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p260#2/r6.claim: The author describes fertilization and embryonic development as fluid mixing, clot, lump, differentiation into organs, and growth of the limbs and internal organs, all formed by God.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p260#2/r6.anchor: فإذا اشتد ذلك الامتزاج وقوي وتمتن حتى استعد لأن يقسم فيه الأعضاء

BIQAI-FULL:v8p263/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p263/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p263/r1.claim: The spirit and body contend: the spirit is perfected while the body bears appetites and low impulses, so God strengthens the spirit through revealed law and prophetic teaching.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p263/r1.anchor: قوى سبحانه الروح بالشرع الداعي إلى معالي الأخلاق

BIQAI-FULL:v8p263/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p263/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p263/r2.claim: ‘We test him’ means God subjects the person to commands, prohibitions, and exhortation as a test in human terms, though God already knows; this establishes proof and makes accountability intelligible to people.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p263/r2.anchor: ونحن أعلم به منه , ولكنا فعلنا ذلك لنقيم عليه الحجة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p263/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p263/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p263/r3.claim: Hearing and sight enable a person to perceive signs and arguments; hearing comes first because it serves address and audible signs are clearer than visible ones.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p263/r3.anchor: وقدم السمع لأنه أنفع في المخاطبات

BIQAI-FULL:v8p263/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p263/r4.speaker: الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p263/r4.claim: Al-Rāzī says the natural report ends here, after which acquired testing begins.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p263/r4.anchor: قال الرازي في اللوامع وإلى هنا انتهى الخبر الفطري

BIQAI-FULL:v8p263/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p263/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p263/r5.claim: The spirit is created after the body is prepared; intellect and five outward senses let people register sensations, avoid harm, seek benefit, and become capable of moral responsibility.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p263/r5.anchor: ثم أفاض سبحانه على الجملة العقل , وجعل السمع والبصر اللتين له

BIQAI-FULL:v8p263/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p263/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p263/r6.claim: The author outlines inward faculties: common sense receives perceptions, imagination stores images, estimation perceives particular meanings, memory stores them, and a combining faculty searches and rearranges them before intellectual knowledge.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p264/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p264/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p264/r1.claim: The inward faculties culminate in acquired intellect, the soul’s active presence of intelligibles and goal of its pursuit; theoretical reason serves practical reason and related faculties.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p264/r1.anchor: وهذا العقل هو غاية السلوك الطلبي للإنسان

DURR-FULL:v8p367/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود في قوله: {أمشاج} قال: العروق

DURR-FULL:v8p367/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r2.claim: The mixed drop consists of male and female fluids mingling.
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {من نطفة أمشاج} قال: من ماء الرجل وماء المرأة حين يختلطان

DURR-FULL:v8p367/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r3.claim: The man's and woman's emissions mingle to form the mixed drop.
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {من نطفة أمشاج} قال: هو نزول الرجل والمرأة يمشج بعضه ببعض

DURR-FULL:v8p367/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the fluids mix in the womb and cites Abu Dhuʾayb's poem, where 'مشيج' means something mixed.
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس إن نافع بن الأزرق قال له: أخبرني عن قوله: {من نطفة أمشاج}

DURR-FULL:v8p367/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r5.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r5.claim: The man's fluid mixes with the woman's and becomes a created being.
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r5.anchor: عن الحسن قال مشج ماء الرجل بماء المرأة فصار خلقا

DURR-FULL:v8p367/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r6.speaker: الربيع
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r6.claim: The combined male and female fluids are called 'أمشاج'.
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r6.anchor: عن الربيع قال: إذا اجتمع ماء الرجل وماء المرأة فهو أمشاج

DURR-FULL:v8p367/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r7.claim: The mixed drop is water and blood together, then develops into a clot and lump.
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r7.anchor: عن قتادة قال: الأمشاج إذا اختلط الماء والدم ثم كان علقة ثم كان مضغة

DURR-FULL:v8p367/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r8.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r8.claim: The human is made from a drop mixed with menstrual blood, which stops when pregnancy occurs.
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r8.anchor: عن الحسن في الآية قال: خلق من نطفة مشجت بدم وذلك الدم الحيض إذا حملت ارتفع الحيض

DURR-FULL:v8p367/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {من نطفة أمشاج} قال: مختلفة الألوان

DURR-FULL:v8p367/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r10.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r10.claim: The drop's colors: male fluid is white and red, female fluid green and red.
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r10.anchor: عن مجاهد {من نطفة أمشاج} قال: ألوان نطفة الرجل بيضاء وحمراء ونطفة المرأة خضراء وحمراء

DURR-FULL:v8p367/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r11.claim: The mixed substance is a string-like piece issuing after urination, from which the child develops.
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: الأمشاج الذي يخرج على أثر البول كقطع الأوتار ومنه يكون الولد

DURR-FULL:v8p367/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r12.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r12.claim: 'أمشاج' means the veins present in semen.
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r12.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم قال: الأمشاج العروق التي في النطفة

DURR-FULL:v8p367/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas also glosses the mixed drop as colors of human creation.
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r13.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {من نطفة أمشاج} قال: ألوان الخلق

DURR-FULL:v8p367/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r14.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r14.claim: Qatada traces development from drop through clot, lump, bone, flesh, and hair; God explains origins to test gratitude and knowledge of His rights, then guides people to gratitude or ingratitude.
DURR-FULL:v8p367/r14.anchor: عن قتادة {إنا خلقنا الإنسان من نطفة أمشاج نبتليه} قال: طورا نطفة وطورا علقة وطورا مضغة

DURR-FULL:v8p368/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p368/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p368/r1.claim: Bones, nerves, and veins come from the man, while flesh, blood, and hair come from the woman.
DURR-FULL:v8p368/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: الأمشاج منه العظام والعصب والعروق من الرجل واللحم والدم والشعر من المرأة

DURR-FULL:v8p368/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p368/r2.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p368/r2.claim: Ikrima specifies fingernail, bone, and nerves from the man; flesh and hair from the woman.
DURR-FULL:v8p368/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة في قوله: {أمشاج} قال: الظفر والعظم والعصب من الرجل واللحم والشعر من المرأة

BURHAN:v4p93#2/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p93#2/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p93#2/r4.claim: Further counterexamples repeat the same definite word for different referents, including the scripture revealed to Muhammad and earlier scripture, and God's sovereignty versus what He grants a servant.
BURHAN:v4p93#2/r4.anchor: فالملك الذي يؤتيه الله للعبد لايمكن إن يكون نفس ملكه فقد اختلفا وهما معرفتان

BURHAN:v2p490/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p490/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p490/r4.claim: Explicit repetition can magnify the matter: it stresses the ease of restoring creation, the greatness of creating humanity, and the terror of the Day when mountains are shaken.

ITQAN:v2p350/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p350/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p350/r8.claim: Amshaj means the mingling of the man's and woman's fluids when they meet in the womb; the text begins to cite Abu Dhuʾayb's poetry as evidence.
ITQAN:v2p350/r8.anchor: قال اختلاط ماء الرجل وماء المرأة إذا وقع في الرحم قال وهل تعرف العرب ذلك قال نعم أما سمعت قول أبي ذؤيب

ITQAN:v2p561/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p561/r1.speaker: الشيخ بهاء الدين
ITQAN:v2p561/r1.claim: Bahāʾ al-Dīn says the rule is unsettled: examples include definite words used for different referents, such as al-insān for Adam and then his offspring, and al-kitāb for Qur'an and earlier scriptures.
ITQAN:v2p561/r1.anchor: قال الشيخ بهاء الدين في عروس الأفراح وغيره إن الظاهر أن هذه القاعدة غير محررة فإنها منتقصة بآيات كثيرة منها في القسم الأول

ITQAN:v2p561/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p561/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p561/r4.claim: Al-Suyūṭī says the examples do not overturn the rule: al- in al-iḥsān, al-nafs, and al-ḥurr is generic and functions semantically like an indefinite; al-ʿusr differs.
ITQAN:v2p561/r4.anchor: لا إنتفاض بشيء من ذلك عند التأمل فإن اللام في الإحسان للجنس فيما يظهر وحينئذ يكون في المعنى كالنكرة وكذا آية النفس والحر بخلاف آية العسر

ITQAN:v3p195/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p195/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p195/r1.claim: Replacing a pronoun with an explicit noun can magnify the matter, as repeating al-insān after first mentioning him does.
ITQAN:v3p195/r1.anchor: ﴿ هل أتى على الإنسان حين من الدهر لم يكن شيئا مذكورا إنا خلقنا الإنسان ﴾

ITQAN:v3p234#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p234#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p234#2/r1.claim: Insijām is smooth, unlabored speech, free of complexity and flowing like water; al-Suyūṭī says the Qur'an as a whole has this quality.
ITQAN:v3p234#2/r1.anchor: هو أن يكون الكلام لخلوه من العقادة منحدرا كتحدر الماء المنسجم ويكاد لسهولة تركيبه وعذوبة ألفاظه أن يسيل رقة والقرآن كله كذلك

ITQAN:v3p234#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p234#2/r2.speaker: أهل البديع
ITQAN:v3p234#2/r2.claim: Badiʿ authorities say strong insijām can make prose read metrically without intention because of its flowing composition.
ITQAN:v3p234#2/r2.anchor: قال أهل البديع وإذا قوى الانسجام في النثر جاءت قراءته موزونة بلا قصد لقوة انسجامه

ITQAN:v3p234#2/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p234#2/r12.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p234#2/r12.claim: He offers the verse's opening as an instance of al-munsariḥ meter.
ITQAN:v3p234#2/r12.anchor: ومن المنسرح ﴿ إنا خلقنا الإنسان من نطفة ﴾

DAMGHANI:v1p69/r5.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p69/r5.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p69/r5.claim: Baṣīr means sight with the eyes; this sense also occurs in the account of Joseph and the description of sharp sight on Judgment Day.

DAMGHANI:v1p246/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p246/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p246/r3.claim: Samʿ can also mean hearing with the ears.
DAMGHANI:v1p246/r3.anchor: الثاني : السمع يعني الأذنين قوله تعالى في سورة الإنسان

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p199/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p199/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p199/r1.claim: Baṣīr is opposite of blind; baṣar can mean sight or knowledge, and baṣīr can mean knowledgeable.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p199/r1.anchor: البصير : ضد الأعمى ، والبصر : واحد الأبصار . والبصر : أيضا العلم بالشيء

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p199/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p199/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p199/r2.claim: Baṣīra can denote a rounded blood drop, a shield, or proof.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p199/r2.anchor: والبصيرة : القطعة من الدم إذا وقعت على الأرض استدارت . والبصيرة : الترس . والبصيرة : البرهان

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p199/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p199/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p199/r3.claim: The verbs baṣura and abṣara can mean knowing and seeing.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p199/r3.anchor: يقال : بصرت بالشيء : إذا صرت بصيرا به عالما

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p199/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p199/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p199/r4.claim: In the cited poem, baṣīr means a dog.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p199/r4.anchor: والبصير : الكلب ، في قول القائل : - أرى نار ليلى أو يراني بصيرها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p199/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p199/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p199/r6.claim: Baṣīr can mean seeing with the eye.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p345/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p345/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p345/r1.claim: Samāʿ is perceiving sounds by hearing; samʿ is the faculty that perceives them.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p345/r1.anchor: السماع : إدراك السمع المسموعات . والسمع : الحاسة المدركة للأصوات

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p345/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p345/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p345/r2.claim: With kasra on sīn, samʿ can mean good renown; it can also denote the offspring of a wolf and hyena.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p345/r2.anchor: والسمع : بكسر السين ، الذكر الجميل ، والسمع أيضا : ولد ( الذئب من الضبع

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p345/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p345/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p345/r3.claim: Samāʿ with fatḥa on sīn and kasra on ʿayn can be an imperative meaning “listen.”
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p345/r3.anchor: ويقال : سماع بفتح السين وكسر العين بمعنى : أسمع

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p345/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p345/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p345/r4.claim: Samāʿ can mean ordinary auditory perception; this is the general sense.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r1.claim: An anonymous poetic line uses مشيج in an image of something mixed or interlaced; the Ẓāhiriyya version preserves a second couplet, while other witnesses retain the first, which contains the word.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r1.anchor: كأن النصل والفوقين منه. . . خلال الريش سيط به مشيج

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r2.speaker: الفراء
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ glosses amshāj as mixtures, including male and female fluids, blood, and a clot; al-Bukhārī gives the same explanation.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r2.anchor: فسره الفراء في معاني القرآن، بالأخلاط، ماء الرجل وماء المرأة والدم والعلقة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r3.speaker: المبرد
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r3.claim: Al-Mubarrad gives the singular as mashj and explains it here as sperm mixed with blood.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r3.anchor: وحكى معه عن المبرد: واحد الأمشاج مشج وهو هنا اختلاط النطفة بالدم

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r4.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r4.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī says a mashīj can consist of two colors and uses both mashj and mashīj for it.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r4.anchor: وفيه عن ابن الأعرابي: يكون مشيج من لونين فهو مشج ومشيج

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r5.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās describes the mixture as red intermingled with white and white with red; another says its colors differ, a view many linguists prefer.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r5.anchor: وفي رواية عن ابن عباس عند القرطبي "الأمشاج الحمرة في البياض والبياض في الحمرة"

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r6.speaker: عكرمة
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r6.claim: ʿIkrima reports that the man contributes skin and bone, while the woman contributes hair and blood.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r6.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم من طريق عكرمة قال: من الرجل الجلدُ والعظم ومن المرأة الشعرُ والدم

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r7.speaker: الحسن
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains the term as seed mixed with the woman’s menstrual blood.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r7.anchor: ومن طريق الحسن: من نطفة مُشِجتْ بدم المرأة وهو دم الحيض

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r8.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r8.speaker: مجاهد
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r8.claim: Mujāhid describes the mixture as red and black.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r8.anchor: ومن طريق ابن جريح عن مجاهد: أحمر وأسود

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r9.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r9.claim: Ibn Masʿūd interprets amshāj as veins.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r9.anchor: وأخرج سعيد بن منصور عن ابن مسعود قال: الأمشاج العروق

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r10.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r10.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r10.claim: Bint al-Shāṭiʾ concludes that these reported explanations all fall within the range of the extended discussions in major tafsirs.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p346/r10.anchor: ولا يخرج عن هذه الأقوال ما في التفاسير الموسعة كالطبري والقرطبي وابن كثير والبحر المحيط

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p345/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p345/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p345/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says amshaj is the man's and woman's fluids mixed together in the womb; he says Arabs knew the term and begins citing Abu Dhu'ayb as evidence.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p345/r7.anchor: قال: ماء الرجل وماء المرأة إذا اجتمعا في الرحم كان مشيجا. قال: وهل كانت العرب تعرف ذلك؟

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#2/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#2/r5.claim: A reported proof that hearing is superior is that no prophet was deaf, though a prophet such as Jacob could become blind after losing his child.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#2/r5.anchor: قالوا: لأن السمع أفضل. قالوا: والدليل على ذلك

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#2/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#2/r6.claim: The author grounds hearing's priority in receiving revelation: a blind person can understand a message like a sighted person, but a deaf person cannot receive it as easily and is farther from understanding.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#2/r6.anchor: فالأصم أنأى عن الفهم من الأعمى، ولذا كان من العميان علماء كبار بخلاف الصم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p482/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p482/r1.speaker: قالوا
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p482/r1.claim: They argue hearing is superior because no prophet was deaf, although a prophet such as Yaqub could be blind; they cite the Qur’an’s repeated ordering of hearing before sight.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p482/r1.anchor: قالوا لأن السمع أفضل. قاولا والدليل على ذلك أن الله تعالى لم يبعث نياً أصم ولكن قد يكون النبي أعمى كيعقوب

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p482/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p482/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p482/r2.claim: Samarrai limits the preference to receiving revelation: a blind person can still understand the message, while deafness makes its delivery and comprehension harder.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p482/r2.anchor: والظاهر أن السمع بالنسبة إلى تلقي الرسالة أفضل من البصر ففاقد البصر يستطيع أن يفهم ويعي مقاصد الرسالة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p908/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p908/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p908/r1.claim: A Quranic pattern avoids directly attributing evil to God while attributing good to Him; examples use passive constructions for harm or evil being willed.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p908/r1.anchor: هناك خط عام في القرآن الكريم وهو أن الله تعالى لا ينسب الشرّ لنفسه مطلقاً

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p908/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p908/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p908/r2.claim: God's punishment and destruction of unbelievers may harm them individually but is a general good and a blessing for people.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p908/r2.anchor: وأخذ الكافرين وإهلاكهم هو من الخير العام وهو نعمة على الناس أصلاً

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p908/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p908/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p908/r3.claim: God's determination of good and evil is a creed safeguard against imagining separate deities for good and evil.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p908/r3.anchor: الخير والشر مُقدّر من الله تعالى وهذا هو يقين العقيدة حتى لا يتبادر إلى ذهن الإنسان أن هناك إله للخير وإله آخر للشرّ

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p908/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p908/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p908/r4.claim: God can say He tested the people of Moses because a test is an ordeal, not evil.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p908/r4.anchor: وهذه الفتنة ليست شراً وإنما هي ابتلاء فالله تعالى خلق الموت والحياة للابتلاء

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p908/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p908/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p908/r5.claim: Testing humanity is one of God's purposes in creation, as stated in 67:2 and 76:2.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p908/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p908/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p908/r6.claim: The Quran says God adorned people's deeds, but never says He adorned their evil deeds, consistent with its careful attribution of evil.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p908/r6.anchor: وفي القرآن يذكر (زيّنا لهم أعمالهم) ولم يرد في القرآن مرة (زينا لهم سوء أعمالهم)

JISHUMI:v10p7199/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7199/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7199/r14.claim: Nuṭfah is man's fluid; originally it means a small amount of water in a container, though it can also refer to more, and its plurals include niṭāf and nuṭaf.
JISHUMI:v10p7199/r14.anchor: والنطفة: ماء الرجل، وأصله: الماء القليل يكون في إناء

JISHUMI:v10p7199/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7199/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7199/r15.claim: Amshāj means mixtures, its singular is mashj, and the verb mashaǧtu means I mixed one thing with another.
JISHUMI:v10p7199/r15.anchor: والأمشاج: الأخلاط، واحدها: مشج، ومشجت هذا بهذا

JISHUMI:v10p7199/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7199/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7199/r16.claim: Ibtalāʾ means testing or choosing; since God cannot literally be tested, He treats people as a tester would so what He already knows becomes manifest.
JISHUMI:v10p7199/r16.anchor: والابتلاء: الاختيار، وحقيقته لا تجوز عليه تعالى، وإنما يعامل معاملة المختبر
